weaknesses: Development is officially paused indefinitely (README banner). There have been no functional commits since 2026-03-04, and the author has moved on to the Quickshell-based DLux.

No NixOS support whatsoever, and the design fights it. customize, apply-colors, update-hyprlock and nekoroshell update all rewrite files inside ~/.config (shims, .sum files, sed -i on hyprlock skins, appending `source =` lines to windowrules.conf). Under Home Manager those paths would be read-only store symlinks. The autostart also hardcodes FHS paths (`/usr/lib/xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland || /usr/libexec/...`), `shell /usr/bin/zsh` in kitty, `/usr/share/zsh-theme-powerlevel10k` in .zshrc, and `XDG_MENU_PREFIX,arch-`.

Hardcoded username paths: `/home/nekorosys/...` appears in waybar config.jsonc, style.css and colors.css, the SwayNC and wlogout style.css imports, and hyprlock.conf. It only works because install.sh runs sed over the tree. The user template also hardcodes `monitor:eeDP-1` (a typo) on workspace 1.

Broken lock-screen theming: both hyprlock skins `source = ~/.cache/wal/colors-hyprland.conf`, a leftover from pywal. wallust actually writes to ~/.cache/wallust/, so mkhmtcore's $wallpaper/$colorN/$background are undefined. The legacy skin uses a CSS-style `border-radius: 50%` inside the hyprlock image block, which isn't valid hyprlock syntax (hyprlock uses `rounding`). It also sets `no_fade_in` and `disable_loading_bar`, which are likely removed or no-ops in current hyprlock (not verified).
Deprecated Hyprland option: nk-gamemode sets `keyword decoration:drop_shadow 0`, which was replaced by `decoration:shadow:enabled` in Hyprland 0.45, so the game-mode toggle leaves shadows on.

check-video.sh passes `--input-ipc-server=$SOCKET` with SOCKET never defined in that script. After a relogin the restored video wallpaper therefore has no IPC socket, and mpvpaper-stop (pointed at /tmp/mpvsocket) can't pause it.

hypr-nice sets clients off the active workspace to nice 19 and later tries to set them back to 0 with setpriority. Without CAP_SYS_NICE or a raised RLIMIT_NICE an unprivileged user can't lower niceness, so windows likely stay at 19 for good. I didn't test this; it's inferred from the Linux permission rules. The same daemon parses JSON by hand and shells out to hyprctl twice per event.

navbar-hover polls `hyprctl cursorpos` through popen every 50ms (about 20 fork/exec calls per second) and checks SwayNC visibility every 200ms. That's wasteful compared with using the Hyprland socket2 events or a layer-shell hotzone.

`borderangle, 1, 30, liner, loop` is set while the border is a single solid color ($color13). The loop does nothing visible but keeps Hyprland redrawing all the time. inactive_opacity 0.3 makes unfocused windows almost unreadable.
hypridle dims at 420s and suspends at 420s, so the dim step is pointless. The lock timer is 300s. after_sleep_cmd restarts the whole bar.

Stale dependency: swww was renamed to awww and moved to Codeberg (its GitHub README says so, citing a 2025-10-29 blog post), yet the installer still runs `cargo install --git https://github.com/LGFae/swww.git`. pkglist-arch uses `rofi-wayland`; I believe upstream rofi now supports Wayland natively, but didn't verify that. There's a leftover `windowrule = center 1, match:class ^(wofi)$` from the wofi era.

Installer fragility: `rm -rf ~/.config/<dir>` before copying (backed up to a tar, but destructive). It references a flatpak.txt that isn't in the repo and a `systemd` config dir that doesn't exist. It needs cargo, go and flatpak just to install three tools. The bundled pkglist-nekoro.txt is the author's full machine (nvidia-580xx-dkms, steam, spotify, calligra), and CI installs GTK/layer-shell headers the code doesn't use.

Theme leaks that bypass wallust: waybar calendar #acb0d0/#41a6b5, SwayNC #45475a, power-profile colors red/green/cornflowerblue, and hardcoded white text-shadows (`0 0 0.3125rem white`) that will look wrong in light mode.

Licensing: the GPL-3.0 repo bundles copyrighted wallpapers with no attribution: My Hero Academia, Bleach, Chainsaw Man (War Devil, Yoru), Studio Ghibli Totoro, four Microsoft Windows 11 stock images, and bad-apple.mp4, plus anime fastfetch PNGs.
Cursor, GTK and Qt theming are absent (Kvantum is still an undecided item on the roadmap). There's no login manager or boot theme, and .zshrc sources powerlevel10k three times.
NVIDIA and Intel specific assumptions: `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD` and `__NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD=1` are always exported in the wallpaper scripts, and the README itself warns about this.
steal_list: Skin architecture: `<app>/skins/<name>/` folders plus a single generated entry file per app (CSS @import, rasi @import, waybar jsonc `include`) with an md5 guard that backs up user edits. On NixOS, generate the entry files into ~/.cache or $XDG_STATE_HOME and have HM-managed configs import from there, so the store files stay immutable.

Each UI skin ships a `layerrule.conf` sourced into Hyprland (blur on, ignore_alpha 0.1-0.6, dim_around on rofi and the control center, `animation slide right 1 4 winIn` for notifications). Blur and motion stay coupled to the skin.

The overshoot curve set for a bouncy, cute feel: wind (0.05,0.9,0.1,1.05), winIn (0.1,1.1,0.1,1.1), winOut (0.3,-0.3,0,1), with popin 90% on layers. Keep a snappy set (0.15,1.0,0.1,1.0) as a "compact/performance" skin. Drop the borderangle loop unless the border is a gradient.

One-click dark/light: two wallust configs (dark16/light16, lab color space) plus semantic text/text-invert tokens appended after generation, exposed as a control-center toggle. Pastel-ify by using higher saturation or a custom template palette.

Rofi wallpaper browser: a 4x3 grid of 120px thumbnails with the dmenu `\0icon\x1f` protocol and async ffmpeg/magick thumbnail caching. Accept pasted URLs and show a notify-send progress bar (x-canonical-private-synchronous + int:value).
Run wallust on the cached 200px thumbnail rather than the full image for fast recoloring, and on an extracted video frame for animated wallpapers.
Video wallpapers with mpvpaper plus mpvpaper-stop (pause when occluded), and runtime GPU detection for hwdec. Use awww (the renamed swww) for stills with its transitions.

A `makenotif` helper with a synchronous replace hint, transient flag, progress and sound, used for every action (theme changed, screenshot taken, download progress) so the system feels responsive and friendly.

A `sys-power` wrapper that abstracts lock/logout/suspend/hibernate across compositor and init. Wire it into wlogout, clickable hyprlock labels (onclick) and hypridle. It works unchanged on Arch and NixOS.
A keybind cheatsheet generated from trailing `# comments` in keybinds.conf (show-keybinds). This could be a small script or a rofi/Quickshell popup.
A hover/dynamic auto-hide bar with activate/deactivate hysteresis, reimplemented event-driven on Hyprland socket2 or natively in Quickshell rather than 50ms hyprctl polling.

A user sandbox: templates copied once into user/configs, which updates never touch, plus hooks (post-install, post-update, on-theme-change). A game-mode toggle through `hyprctl --batch` using current option names (decoration:shadow:enabled).

A SwayNC control center with a pill buttons grid (wifi, bt, DND, contrast, hyprsunset night light), mpris with rounded art, and a gradient-to-accent footer. Combine with a hyprsunset profile (20:00, 4350K, gamma 0.9).

Installer ideas worth porting to an Arch bootstrap script: --dry-run, a tar backup, laptop detection that adds `gesture = 3, horizontal, workspace` lines, and monitor placeholder detection via hyprctl or /sys/class/drm.

one_line: A small, very polished Arch-only Hyprland rice. It uses the new Hyprland 0.55+ Lua config and a hand-written Quickshell shell: a bar, a launcher that morphs out of the screen edge, notifications, a power menu, and media and CPU/RAM cards that show only on an empty desktop. A theme-switcher carousel recolours Hyprland borders and kitty and changes the wallpaper from a small JSON theme file. It ships two themes: Girls' Last Tour (warm sepia and gold) and Shorekeeper (dusk purple).
freshness: Very new and active. All commits visible on the GitHub commits page are dated Sep 8-9, 2026, the latest being "Merge pull request #1 from Cenaure/dev" on Sep 9, 2026. That makes the repo about 2.5 weeks old on 2026-09-25. It has 4 stars and 0 forks, and an MIT license (Copyright 2026 Cenaure). It targets bleeding-edge software: Hyprland's Lua config (added in 0.55, which deprecates hyprlang per hypr.land/news/26_lua) and `awww`, the renamed swww (moved to Codeberg in Oct 2025 per LGFae's blog). A Sep 8 commit is titled "feat: add lock-screen and power-menu", but there is NO lock-screen module in the HEAD tree. Only the power menu exists, and a leftover comment in services/Theme.qml still refers to a lock screen.

aesthetic.palette: The colours come from a hand-picked JSON theme with 7 roles (background, surface, foreground, foregroundSurface, active, secondary, disabled) plus a 'kitty' sub-block. GIRLS LAST TOUR (sepia/gold): surface #2a2723, foreground #332f27, foregroundSurface #e0d7c6, active #d9a441, secondary #9a896f, disabled #6b6459, background 'transparent'; kitty: surface #29221d, fg #ede3d1, active #d9a441, secondary #6e6251, disabled #4f4b46. SHOREKEEPER BLUE (actually lavender/purple): surface #2b243d, foreground/foregroundSurface #ebd7f5, active #bf7ee0, secondary #5d578c, disabled #606275; kitty: surface #202033, fg #e9e6f7, active #867ee0, secondary #5d578c, disabled #606275. Hyprland fallback borders: gradient rgba(5b7fa6ff)->rgba(3a5270ff) at 135deg, inactive rgba(2a335055). The generated GLT borders are rgba(d9a441ff)->rgba(9a896fff) at 135deg, inactive rgba(6b645955). Some colours are hardcoded outside the themes: urgent/critical/temp-warning #e0707e, low battery #e0b070. Kitty's base palette, 'Nightshade Drift': bg #232330, selection #45364B, fg #E0D7E5, dim #A394A8, cursor #8D6B94, active border #62466B, inactive border #2e2e3d, bell #D05A8E. ANSI colours: 0/8 #232330/#45364B, 1/9 #D05A8E/#D96FA0, 2/10 #7A8F6F/#96AA89, 3/11 #B89A6A/#D4B484, 4/12 #5A6FA8/#7088C4, 5/13 #8D6B94/#A67FAE, 6/14 #5E8A94/#75A8B4, 7/15 #A394A8/#E0D7E5.
aesthetic.color_pipeline: A custom script pipeline, with no matugen/pywal/wallust. services/Theme.qml (a Quickshell singleton) finds every themes/*.json using a FolderListModel, so adding a theme is just dropping in a file. It saves the chosen id to state/current-theme.state.json. On a switch it: (1) runs `awww img <wallpaper> --transition-type wipe --transition-fps 60 --transition-duration 1`; (2) runs scripts/apply-theme.bash <id>. That script runs every scripts/themes/*.bash (one per app), collects failures, and reports them to stderr / console.warn. change-hyprland-colors.bash uses jq to read active/secondary/disabled and checks each is a #RRGGBB value. It writes hypr/modules/colors.lua atomically (mktemp + mv), refuses to install the file if `luac -p` fails, then applies live with `hyprctl eval "hl.config({...})"` (hyprctl keyword does not work under the Lua config). change-kitty-colors.bash writes kitty/colors/colors.conf, which overrides only the theme's roles on top of base.conf. The accent replaces color5/color13, then it sends `pkill -USR1 -x kitty` to live-reload. QML widgets bind directly to Services.Theme.* through per-module config singletons. GTK is fixed at adw-gtk3 prefer-dark, and Qt uses qt6ct; neither is recoloured by the pipeline.
aesthetic.fonts: UI (bar, launcher, notifications, power menu, stats): 'AnnotationM Nerd Font' (Arch package ttf-annotationmono-nerd). Icons: 'Material Symbols Outlined' (bar, launcher, notifications; AUR ttf-material-symbols-variable-git) and 'Material Symbols Rounded' (media transport). Media card text: 'Adwaita Sans' (adwaita-fonts). Track titles containing kana or kanji switch to 'Noto Sans CJK JP'. Terminal: 'JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono' at size 13. App glyphs in workspace slots come from a Nerd Font class-to-glyph map in BarConfig.appIcons.
aesthetic.icons_cursor_gtk_qt: GTK: `gsettings color-scheme prefer-dark` and gtk-theme 'adw-gtk3' (adw-gtk-theme package). Qt: QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt6ct. qt5ct, qt6ct and kvantum are installed but the repo ships no qt6ct or kvantum config. Icon theme: only breeze-icons is installed, and no icon theme is set. Cursor: only XCURSOR_SIZE and HYPRCURSOR_SIZE = 20 are set; no cursor theme is named or installed. Shell icons are Material Symbols glyphs plus Nerd Font app glyphs, not an icon theme.
aesthetic.geometry: Hyprland: gaps_in 6, gaps_out 10, border_size 1 (gradient 135deg), rounding 10, rounding_power 5 (squircle-ish), active_opacity 1.0, inactive_opacity 0.9. Shadow: enabled, range 4, render_power 3, color rgba(1a1a1aee). Blur: enabled, size 3, passes 1, vibrancy 0.1696. resize_on_border and allow_tearing are true; layout dwindle with preserve_split. Spotify rule: opacity 0.85/0.7, rounding 12. Fullscreen rule: no blur/shadow/dim/anim, rounding 0. Quickshell: the bar is transparent, height 40, margins [10,15,0,15], and every widget is a floating pill with radius height/2. Workspace track: pill with padding 4. Slots: h24, w30, padding 8, spacing 2, up to 3 app icons per slot plus a '+N' overflow; the sliding capsule animates in 220ms OutCubic. Bar popups: radius 16, padding 8, row height 30, row radius 10, gap 16, rising 8px over 180ms. Launcher: 560 wide, radius 26, padding 14, flush with the bottom edge with square bottom corners, morphing out of a 220x46 anchor in 320ms; rows 46px radius 12, 7 visible rows, selection = accent at 0.18 alpha. Notification cards: 380 wide, radius 20, padding 14, a 3px urgency accent stripe, slide in 40px over 260ms. Notification centre: 440 wide, radius 28, flush bottom, 360ms. Theme switcher: 520 wide, radius 28; thumbnails 152x86 radius 10, inactive scale 0.84 and opacity 0.5; swatches 18px radius 6. Media and stats cards: radius 28, padding 18; progress/usage bars 4px high radius 2; the per-core strip is 18px tall. Power menu: three 116x116 tiles, 1px border, 18 spacing, sliding up from the bottom. Kitty: window_padding_width 18, background_opacity 0.8, cursor_shape beam, cursor_trail 3, hidden scrollbars, url_style curly.
aesthetic.animations: Hyprland Lua beziers: ivory (0.23,1.00),(0.32,1.00) [easeOutQuint]; felt (0.16,0.80),(0.25,1.00); damper (0.40,0.00),(1.00,1.00) [ease-in]; sustain (0.45,0.05),(0.55,0.95); resonance (0.25,0.46),(0.45,0.94); linear. Leaves: global 10 default. Windows: windows 5 ivory; windowsIn 5 ivory slide; windowsOut 3 damper slide; windowsMove 5 ivory. Borders: border 7 sustain; borderangle 6 linear (not looping). Fades: fade 4 sustain; fadeIn 3.5 ivory; fadeOut 3 damper; fadeDim 5 sustain; fadeShadow 4 sustain; fadeSwitch 3.5 felt. Layers: layers 5 ivory; layersIn 5 felt fade; layersOut 3 damper fade; fadeLayersIn 4 ivory; fadeLayersOut 3 damper. Workspaces: workspaces, In and Out all 6 ivory slide. Special workspace: 5.5 ivory slidevert; In 5.5 felt slidevert; Out 4 damper slidevert. zoomFactor 9 resonance. In QML, FloatingPanel animates width (OutQuint when opening, InOutQuad when closing), height at 1.1x the width duration so it looks like unfolding, and radius at 0.8x OutCubic. Contents fade in after a pause of 45% of the duration. Slide-in panels use Translate y with OutQuint in and InCubic out. The desktop card row reflows in 320ms.
aesthetic.wallpapers: Two PNGs in .config/quickshell/wallpapers/: girls_last_tour.png (fan art of Chito and Yuuri from Girls' Last Tour, visibly signed 'Dabaka') and shorekeeper.png (art of Shorekeeper from Wuthering Waves, captioned 'SHOREKEEPER // THENOTOSEED' and signed/dated 2025.2.1x). Both are third-party illustrations bundled in an MIT repo with no credit or licence notice. The wallpaper is part of each theme and is set through awww with a 60fps wipe transition.
aesthetic.vibe: From the two README screenshots I viewed: minimal and cozy, with a 'floating pills on the wallpaper' layout. Clock and date sit top-left as plain text, a centred workspace pill has app glyphs and a gold or lavender active capsule, and wifi, volume and battery are small round pills top-right. On an empty workspace, a media card (album art, CJK-aware title, progress) and a CPU/RAM card with a per-core strip hang under the bar. It is clean, restrained, and cohesive. The GLT theme is warm sepia with a gold accent. The Shorekeeper theme is dark indigo with a lavender accent, which reads as the more cute/pastel of the two. The polish is in the motion and interaction: morphing panels, a sliding capsule, and a layout OSD at the cursor. It is not maximalist: 1px borders, light blur, and no glass or blur on the shell surfaces, which are opaque. I'd rate it high on taste and engineering and moderate on eye-candy density. It is a strong base for a 'cute but classy' rice rather than a finished, full-featured one.

components.compositor: Hyprland, configured entirely in Lua (.config/hypr/hyprland.lua plus 13 `require`d modules: monitors, programs, autostart, env, permissions, decoration, performance, animations, window_rules, layout, misc, input, keybinds). It uses the hl.config / hl.bind / hl.dsp.* / hl.curve / hl.animation / hl.window_rule / hl.on('hyprland.start') API, so it needs Hyprland 0.55+. Theme colours come from a generated modules/colors.lua loaded with pcall, with a fallback if it is missing.
components.bar_or_shell: A hand-written Quickshell (QML) shell. shell.qml instantiates Bar, Media, SystemStats, ThemeSwitcher, AppLauncher, PowerMenu, LayoutOsd, NotificationPopup and NotificationCenter. Bar layout: Date on the left; HyprlandWorkspaces in the centre; SystemTray, Network (wifi list popup with a password field), Audio (popup with a slider and pavucontrol) and Battery (UPower, Material Symbols level glyphs) on the right. Code is split into services/ (singletons), configurations/ (design tokens per module) and components/ (FloatingPanel, BarPopup, Pill, LevelSlider, MenuList, IconButton, AppIcon, Poller). Panels are toggled over IPC with `qs ipc call <target> toggle`.
components.launcher: Quickshell AppLauncher (modules/app-launcher, services/AppLauncher.qml). It uses fuzzysort.js for fuzzy search and saves state to state/app-launcher.state.json. A qalc (libqalculate) calculator row is debounced at 120ms and runs only when the query looks like maths; it supports unit and currency conversion. A clipboard-history mode is backed by cliphist, fed by `wl-paste --type text|image --watch cliphist store`. The launcher morphs up out of a pill on the bottom screen edge. It opens with SUPER + SUPER_L.
components.notifications: Quickshell NotificationServer (services/Notifications.qml), with state saved to state/notifications.state.json. Popup cards stack under the right end of the bar and slide in from the right. They have a 3px urgency stripe (low = disabled, normal = active, critical = #e0707e), a 36px icon with radius 12, action pills, and a close button. A notification centre (SUPER+N) rises from the bottom edge with a bell/DND toggle, clear-all, and an empty state reading 'Nothing to catch up on'. install.sh masks dunst, mako and swaync so Quickshell owns org.freedesktop.Notifications.
components.lock_idle_logout: There is only a Quickshell power menu (SUPER+M) replacing wlogout. It has three tiles, Lock (L), Shutdown (S) and Restart (R), with no logout or suspend. Lock runs `loginctl lock-session`, but HEAD has no lock screen (no WlSessionLock module, hyprlock or swaylock) and no idle daemon (no hypridle), so as shipped Lock probably does nothing. The commit history mentions an 'add lock-screen' commit, but that module is not in the current tree.
components.wallpaper_tool: awww (swww renamed): `awww-daemon` runs at start, and `awww img` with a wipe transition at 60fps over 1s runs on theme change.
components.terminal: kitty. It includes colors/base.conf (hand-tuned 'Nightshade Drift' 16-colour palette) and then the generated colors/colors.conf. Settings: JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono 13, background_opacity 0.8, window_padding_width 18, beam cursor, cursor_trail 3, curly URL underline, hidden scrollbars, repaint_delay 8, input_delay 3, sync_to_monitor no, shell_integration disabled.
components.shell_prompt: kitty sets `shell fish`, but the repo has no fish config and no prompt (starship, etc.), and fish is not in the install package list.
components.editor: None configured in the repo.
components.file_manager: nautilus (with gvfs, and udiskie for automounting), opened with SUPER+E.
components.fetch: None.
components.login_boot: None: no display manager, GRUB/Limine/systemd-boot theme, or Plymouth.
components.extras: Screenshots with hyprshot-git (PRINT = window, SUPER+PRINT = output, SUPER+SHIFT+S = region). cliphist clipboard history. hyprpolkitagent started through a systemd user unit. udiskie. brightnessctl, including a hardcoded asus::kbd_backlight. playerctl and wpctl for media and volume keys. pavucontrol. A keyboard-layout OSD pill appears next to the pointer while Alt is held, or after a layout switch between us, ru, ua and sk. On empty workspaces only, a media card and a system-stats card (CPU% with temperature warning at 80C, RAM, per-core strip) appear. A theme-switcher carousel (SUPER+T) shows thumbnails and palette swatches. There is no spicetify, cava, Firefox theme or Discord theme. The repo also has a format.sh dev helper that runs prettier, qmlformat, stylua and shfmt.

standout_features: One of the earliest public rices on Hyprland's new Lua config (0.55+). It is modular (hyprland.lua `require`s 13 modules), uses readable hl.curve / hl.animation / hl.window_rule tables, and builds the workspace binds in a `for i = 1, 10` loop. hl.on('hyprland.start', fn) replaces exec-once.

Generated colours are loaded safely: decoration.lua does `local ok, generated = pcall(require, "modules.colors")` and falls back to built-in defaults, so a broken theme file cannot stop Hyprland from starting.

Live recolouring of Hyprland from the shell uses `hyprctl eval "hl.config({ general = { col = {...} } })"`, because `hyprctl keyword` refuses to work under the Lua parser. The generated Lua is checked with `luac -p` before being moved into place.

FloatingPanel.qml is a generic 'widget becomes the menu' morph. One rounded rectangle starts at the exact geometry and radius of the bar pill, then grows to the panel size: width uses OutQuint, height takes 1.1x as long so it unfolds, and radius takes 0.8x. It cross-fades from opacity 0, and contents fade in after 45% of the duration. growUp mode anchors panels flush with the bottom edge with square bottom corners, so they appear to rise out of the screen edge. slideIn mode handles surfaces with no widget to grow from, such as the power menu.

The workspace pill shows up to 3 app glyphs per workspace plus '+N', keeps 6 fixed slots plus any extra real workspaces, and animates a capsule highlight positioned through per-delegate Bindings. It reads toplevel.wayland.appId before lastIpcObject.class to work around empty IPC data for new windows.

'Desktop' widgets appear only when the focused workspace has no windows (services/Desktop.qml). A media card and a CPU/RAM/per-core stats card sit side by side under the bar, match heights, and re-centre with a 320ms reflow when the media card comes or goes. The media card reveals its transport controls on hover.

Adding a theme means dropping in a JSON file: a FolderListModel plus Instantiator indexes themes/*.json automatically for the carousel (thumbnails scaled 0.84 when inactive, palette swatches). apply-theme.bash then runs every per-app script in scripts/themes/, so theming a new app means adding one script.

A keyboard-layout OSD pill follows the cursor. Holding Alt fires `hl.bind("ALT_L", hl.dsp.global("quickshell:layoutPeek"), { non_consuming = true })` over the global-shortcuts protocol. The pointer position is polled from Hyprland's request socket ('cursorpos') every 33ms, but only while the OSD is tracking.
A workspace guard in FloatingPanel undoes Hyprland's focus restore after an exclusive keyboard grab ends. Without it, switching workspace while a panel is open drags you back to where it was opened.
The launcher has a debounced qalc calculator (only when the query looks like maths) and a cliphist clipboard mode. Clipboard ids are passed as argv, not spliced into a shell string.
Per-string CJK font selection for media titles: a regex detects kana or kanji and switches the whole title to 'Noto Sans CJK JP', avoiding fontconfig picking Korean glyph forms.

install.sh is careful. It has --dry-run, a confirmation prompt, timestamped backups to ~/.config-backup/, per-config relinking, and `ln -sfn` (with a comment on why). It bootstraps yay-bin with makepkg when no AUR helper exists, because the icon font is AUR-only, and masks dunst/mako/swaync so Quickshell can own the notification bus.
structure_install: Layout: .config/{hypr,kitty,quickshell}, .github/ (13 screenshots plus a sticker), install.sh, format.sh, plus .prettierrc, .qmlformat.ini and .stylua.toml, and an MIT LICENSE. hypr/ contains hyprland.lua and modules/*.lua. quickshell/ contains shell.qml, components/, configurations/ (one design-token singleton per feature: Bar, AppLauncher, Audio, Desktop, KeyboardLayout, Media, Network, Notifications, PowerMenu, SystemStats, ThemeSwitcher), modules/ (UI), services/ (data singletons: AppLauncher, Audio, Calculator, ClipboardHistory, Cursor, Desktop, KeyboardLayout, MediaPlayer, Network, Notifications, SystemUsage, Theme), scripts/ (apply-theme.bash and themes/change-{hyprland,kitty}-colors.bash), state/*.json (runtime state, committed), themes/*.json and wallpapers/*.png. To install: `git clone ... && ./install.sh -p`. The script symlinks each directory under .config/ into ~/.config, so the repo stays the only copy; with -p it first installs the packages with yay or paru (bootstrapping yay-bin if needed), or with pacman for repo packages only. It targets Arch only and dies if pacman is missing. Repo packages: hyprland, quickshell, awww, kitty, wl-clipboard, cliphist, libqalculate, jq, nautilus, gvfs, udiskie, hyprpolkitagent, brightnessctl, playerctl, wireplumber, pipewire-pulse, pavucontrol, xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland, qt5ct, qt6ct, kvantum, breeze-icons, gsettings-desktop-schemas, adw-gtk-theme, ttf-annotationmono-nerd, adwaita-fonts, ttf-jetbrains-mono-nerd, noto-fonts-cjk. AUR packages: hyprshot-git, ttf-material-symbols-variable-git. There is no NixOS or Nix support at all.

key_snippets.purpose: Named bezier set in Hyprland's Lua syntax (ivory = easeOutQuint) and how the leaves use them
Loads generated theme colours with pcall and a fallback, plus the exact look-and-feel numbers
The whole theme format: 7 semantic roles, a wallpaper, and kitty overrides
Atomic, validated write of the generated Lua and a live apply through hyprctl eval (the Lua config rejects hyprctl keyword)
key_snippets.excerpt:
# Refuse to install a file Lua cannot load, so a bad write can never take the
# Hyprland config down with it.
if command -v luac >/dev/null && ! luac -p "$TMP" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "change-hyprland-colors: generated colors.lua is not valid Lua, keeping the old one" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mv -- "$TMP" "$OUT"
trap - EXIT

# Apply to the running compositor. `hyprctl keyword` refuses to work under the
# Lua parser --- it tells you to use eval --- and a full `hyprctl reload` would
# re-run every bind and submap definition just to change two colours.
if command -v hyprctl >/dev/null && [[ -n ${HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE:-} ]]; then
    hyprctl eval "hl.config({ general = { col = {
        active_border = { colors = { \"$ACTIVE_RGBA\", \"$SECONDARY_RGBA\" }, angle = $ANGLE },
        inactive_border = \"$INACTIVE_RGBA\",
    } } })" >/dev/null
fi

key_snippets.purpose: The morph: one rectangle animates from the pill's size and radius to the panel's, with squared bottom corners so it sits flush on the edge
Lua keybinds: a workspace loop, Alt-hold peek over the global-shortcuts protocol, and the replacements for the old bindm/bindel
key_snippets.excerpt:
for i = 1, 10 do
    local key = i % 10 -- 10 maps to key 0
    hl.bind(mainMod .. " + " .. key, hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = i }))
    hl.bind(mainMod .. " + ALT + " .. key, hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = i }))
end

hl.bind(mainMod .. " + mouse_down", hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = "e+1" }))
hl.bind(mainMod .. " + mouse_up", hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = "e-1" }))

hl.bind("ALT_L", hl.dsp.global("quickshell:layoutPeek"), { non_consuming = true })

hl.bind(mainMod .. " + mouse:272", hl.dsp.window.drag(), { mouse = true })
hl.bind(mainMod .. " + mouse:273", hl.dsp.window.resize(), { mouse = true })

hl.bind("XF86AudioRaiseVolume", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("wpctl set-volume -l 1 @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ 5%+"), { locked = true, repeating = true })
hl.bind("XF86AudioNext", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("playerctl next"), { locked = true })

weaknesses: Arch only, with no NixOS path. install.sh dies without pacman. It also needs Hyprland 0.55+ with the Lua config, so it will not run on older or stable Hyprland packages or on hyprland.conf setups.

The config is tightly tied to Hyprland Lua dispatch. BarConfig.hyprlandLuaConfig is hardcoded to true and dispatch strings are Lua (`hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = N })`). The code notes that Quickshell's Hyprland.usingLua wrongly reports false, so this cannot be detected automatically.

Lock does not work as shipped. The power menu runs `loginctl lock-session`, but HEAD has no lock screen and no idle daemon (no hyprlock, hypridle or WlSessionLock module). The power menu also lacks Logout and Suspend.

Runtime-written files are tracked in git through the symlink install: state/*.json, hypr/modules/colors.lua and kitty/colors/colors.conf. Every theme switch or launch dirties the repo. Under a read-only Nix store this design would break unless the files are linked with mkOutOfStoreSymlink.

Hardcoded, personal values: monitors.lua forces `mode="1920x1080"` at scale 1.0 on all outputs (output=""), which is wrong for HiDPI or high-refresh screens. The keyboard backlight device `asus::kbd_backlight` is hardcoded. kb_layout is 'us,ru,ua,sk'. A leftover default device rule for 'epic-mouse-v1' remains.

The Spotify window rule has a duplicate `match` key in one Lua table literal (harmless, since the last one wins, but sloppy). QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME is set twice (env.lua and hyprland.lua). The gsettings `hl.exec_cmd` calls are at the top level of hyprland.lua rather than inside hl.on('hyprland.start'), so as written they are not limited to startup.

The theme system is shallow. There are only 7 roles and no wallpaper-derived generation (no matugen). GTK (adw-gtk3), Qt (qt6ct and kvantum are installed but not configured), icons (breeze), cursor (size only, no theme) and fish are not themed. Some colours are hardcoded outside themes (#e0707e, #e0b070). The 'foreground' role is dark in GLT but light in Shorekeeper, which is confusing.

It is visually quite understated for 'maximum cute': 1px borders, blur size 3 with passes 1, and no layer blur rules for the Quickshell namespaces, so shell surfaces are opaque rather than glassy. The borderangle animation does not loop.

Wallpaper and theme licensing: girls_last_tour.png (signed 'Dabaka') and shorekeeper.png (captioned 'SHOREKEEPER // THENOTOSEED', artist-signed) are third-party fan art and game-character art. They are redistributed in an MIT repo without credit or permission notes.

kitty sets `shell fish`, but fish is not in the package list and there is no shell or prompt config. Screenshots rely on the AUR package hyprshot-git, and the icon font is AUR-only (ttf-material-symbols-variable-git), which is why install.sh has to bootstrap yay.

Small hacks: Theme.qml's delay() builds a Timer with Qt.createQmlObject for a 10ms deferral. Cursor.qml polls cursorpos every 33ms, which is gated to when the OSD needs it but is still polling. The repo is very young (2 days of commits, 4 stars), so it is not proven over time.
steal_list: Adopt the FloatingPanel morph pattern for the shell. Every popup grows out of the exact pill it belongs to: width OutQuint, height at 1.1x the duration, radius at 0.8x, a cross-fade from 0, and contents delayed by 45%. Bottom surfaces (launcher, notification centre, power menu) sit flush with the screen edge with square bottom corners.

Keep one design-token singleton per feature (configurations/*Config.qml) that binds colours to a Theme singleton. All radii, paddings and durations live in one place, which makes retuning the whole rice for 'cuter' (bigger radii, softer curves) trivial.

Use the theme dispatcher architecture: themes/*.json is picked up automatically, and apply-theme.bash runs scripts/themes/*.bash, one per app. Collect failures, write atomically with mktemp + mv, and validate first (`luac -p`, a hex regex). For the best-of-breed version, feed it from matugen so the JSON is generated from the wallpaper.

For a Hyprland 0.55+ Lua config: split into required modules, load generated colours with `pcall(require, 'modules.colors')` and fallback defaults, and apply colour changes live with `hyprctl eval "hl.config({...})"` instead of reloading.

Reuse the bezier vocabulary: ivory (0.23,1,0.32,1) for in and move, felt (0.16,0.8,0.25,1) for layers and special workspaces, damper (0.4,0,1,1) for out, sustain (0.45,0.05,0.55,0.95) for fades and borders. Use slidevert for the scratchpad.
Show widgets only on an empty desktop: media and stats cards appear when the focused workspace has no toplevels, re-centre as a row, and the media card reveals its transport on hover.
Build a workspace pill with per-workspace app glyphs (max 3 + '+N') and a sliding accent capsule; prefer wayland.appId over lastIpcObject.class.
Add a keyboard-layout OSD at the cursor through `hl.bind('ALT_L', hl.dsp.global('quickshell:layoutPeek'), { non_consuming = true })`. It suits multilingual users.
Give the launcher extras: a qalc calculator (debounced, gated by a looks-like-maths regex) and a cliphist history mode with ids passed as argv.

Copy the install.sh ergonomics for the Arch side: dry-run, confirmation, timestamped backups, `ln -sfn`, yay-bin bootstrap, and masking dunst/mako/swaync so a shell-native notification server owns the bus.
Pick CJK fonts per string for media titles (regex, then 'Noto Sans CJK JP'). It is a nice touch for an anime-themed rice.
Use the kitty details: cursor_trail 3, window_padding_width 18, background_opacity 0.8, and a base.conf plus generated colors.conf split with live reload via `pkill -USR1 kitty`.

When porting to NixOS: link the Quickshell and hypr directories with home-manager `mkOutOfStoreSymlink` (or keep generated files and state under $XDG_STATE_HOME) because the theme switcher writes into its own config tree. I did not verify whether home-manager's Hyprland module supports hyprland.lua; plan to ship it as a raw xdg.configFile.

one_line: A small, personal X11 rice for Arch: BSPWM, Polybar, sxhkd, picom (ibhagwan fork), rofi, dunst and kitty on Dracula colours with some pink and purple accents. It has no Hyprland, no Wayland, no Nix and no installer, so as a reference for a Hyprland rice that targets both Arch and NixOS it is mostly useful for a few pastel colour ideas and polybar/rofi script patterns.
freshness: The repo has 68 commits, 2 stars and 1 fork, and the description is "Dotfiles for my Arch Linux setup". Topics: arch-dotfiles, arch-linux, bspwm. There were active bursts from Oct 2021 to Aug 2023, mostly commits named "Complete overhaul of the repo". After that: Aug 5 2024 "Add files via upload", Sep 26 2024 "Delete .config/yay directory", Jan 2 2025 "Create pacman.conf", and Apr 13 2026 "updates" / "changes & updates". The newest file is etc/pacman.conf, which includes `DownloadUser = alpm` (added in pacman 7), so that file is recent. The desktop configs are much older: Nerd Fonts v2 codepoints (墳, ﬘, 祝, 雷), picom `experimental-backends`, and dunst `geometry`/`shrink` all predate 2022-2023. No license file was seen. The README is only a title plus two screenshots and a wallpaper link.

aesthetic.palette: Mostly Dracula. .Xresources and kitty/dracula.conf: bg #282A36, fg #F8F8F2, red #FF5555, green #50FA7B, yellow #F1FA8C, purple #BD93F9, pink #FF79C6, cyan #8BE9FD, color8 #4D4D4D (kitty uses #6272a4), color0 #000000 (kitty uses #21222c). bspwm borders: normal #44475a, active #bd93f9, focused #ff79c6, presel #6272a4. Polybar: fg #adb1b9, dark-light #272A2B, active-light #313435, now-playing #B589D6, battery ramp #A0E8A2, bluetooth-on #2193ff, speed-down #8dc776, speed-up #c26f6f, temp-warn #c7254f; the bg is read from xrdb. Kitty tab bar (a separate slate/periwinkle set): active #afc3fb on #1d2030, inactive #8189ac on #3c414c; window borders #1d212a / #272c38. Rofi main config.rasi defines lightpink #ffb6c1, darkpink #e75480, lightpurple #b19cd9, mediumpurple #9370DB, plus Nord colours (#2e3440 #eceff4 #bf616a #d08770 #ebcb8b #a3be8c #8fbcbb). The window is #000000aa and the selected row is @lightpurple. Rofi colour schemes: sidebar-dark (accent #d89495, bg #1d212a, fg #f9f9f9, on #2be491, off #4c566a); sidebar light, the cutest one (accent #cf8ef4, bg #f9f9f9, fg #fa74b2, off #dddddd); fullscreen-dark (accent #63c5ea, bg #20242d, bg-light #272c38, focus #434c5e). Dunst: bg #20242d, fg #edfefe, frame #9a9fa0. Cava 8-stop gradient: #80a0ff #74b2ff #79dac8 #85dc85 #36c692 #f09479 #e2637f #ff5189. Polywins: active #e74c5c, inactive #6bb05d. Spicetify: Dribbblish, color_scheme=purple.
aesthetic.color_pipeline: Static colours, no generator (no pywal, wallust or matugen). .Xresources holds the Dracula palette and polybar reads it with ${xrdb:colorN}. Everything else is hand-coded hex in each app: kitty includes dracula.conf, rofi imports colorschemes/*.rasi through one colors.rasi switch file, and dunst, bspwm and cava use literal hex. There are 11 kitty colour schemes (gruvbox, onedark, solarized, misty, Oblivion, a pywal export 'brandon-griggs-wal.conf'…) but only dracula.conf is included. The colours therefore do not match across apps: Dracula in the terminal and WM, Nord-grey in dunst/rofi, a blue-cyan accent in the rofi fullscreen scheme.
aesthetic.fonts: Polybar: 'Iosevka Nerd Font:style=Bold:pixelsize=11;3', 'JetBrainsMono Nerd Font:size=15;3', 'Material Design Icons:style=Bold:size=13;3', 'Dejavu Serif:size=10;3'. Kitty: 'Jetbrains Mono' 11.7, underline cursor with thickness 1.2. Rofi: 'Jetbrains Mono 10'; the sxhkd launcher passes 'JetBrainsMono Italic 10'. Rofi sidebar/power menus: 'Comfortaa 12' text with 'feather 18' icon font, which is a nice cute rounded choice. Dunst: 'Iosevka FT 9'. Betterlockscreen: 'sans-serif'.
aesthetic.icons_cursor_gtk_qt: Very little. Rofi uses icon-theme 'Adwaita'. The dunst icon_path to Papirus-Custom is commented out. The cursor is only set with `xsetroot -cursor_name left_ptr`. There is no GTK or Qt theme, no gtk-3.0 settings, no kvantum/qt5ct and no cursor theme in the repo. Neofetch reports the GTK theme but nothing configures one.
aesthetic.geometry: bspwm: border_width 1, window_gap 5, top_padding 20, split_ratio 0.50, gapless_monocle true, borderless_monocle false, focus_follows_pointer true. picom (ibhagwan/sdhand fork keys): corner-radius 15.0, round-borders 1, round-borders-rule 3px XTerm/URxvt, 10px Alacritty, 15px Signal; rounding is excluded for firefox, chromium, Alacritty, URxvt, XTerm and Thunderbird. Shadow = false (shadow-radius 7, offsets -7/-7 unused). inactive-opacity 0.8, frame-opacity 0.7, active 1.0. Opacity rules: kitty 60, Polybar 60, Code 80, TelegramDesktop 70, discord 80, firefox/chromium 100. Blur is method kawase, strength 7, but background=false, so in practice nothing is blurred. backend glx, vsync true. Polybar: height 15 with border-top/bottom 7 in the bg colour (about 29px effective), width 100%, full-width flat top bar, line-size 1, '|' separators. Kitty: background_opacity 0.9 (stacked under picom's 60% rule), window_padding 10 20 10 20, border 1.0, tab bar 'fade' style with powerline-style templates. Rofi: window border-radius 5px, padding 30px, width 30%, elements radius 5px and padding 10px; appsmenu uses 8px radius; sidebar menu is 6% x 40% anchored east. Dunst: geometry '300x6-16+40', padding 12, frame_width 5, corner_radius 0, separator_height 4.
aesthetic.animations: No animation curves: this is X11 and picom fork has no bezier animations. Only picom fading is set (fading=true, fade-in-step 0.03, fade-out-step 0.03), and `wintypes normal = { fade = false }` turns fading off for normal windows, so only tooltips and popups fade. Kitty tab_bar_style fade with tab_fade 0. Polybar now-playing text scrolls (update_delay 0.3s, 20-char window). Battery charging animation at 750ms per frame.
aesthetic.wallpapers: One bundled wallpaper: images/house-in-the-forest-3840×2160.jpg, linked from the README. The raw URL returned 404 because of the '×' character, so I could not check its contents or where it came from, and no artist credit or license is given. It is restored with `nitrogen --restore`; betterlockscreen uses `feh --bg-fill`. There is also a commented-out `xwallpaper --zoom ~/wall/forest1.png`.
aesthetic.vibe: A typical 2021-2022 r/unixporn beginner/intermediate BSPWM rice: a flat full-width polybar full of Nerd-font icons, 15px rounded windows through the picom fork, a semi-transparent Dracula kitty, and a cozy forest-house wallpaper. It is tidy but not especially cute or polished. The cutest parts are the rofi 'sidebar' light scheme (#f9f9f9 bg, #fa74b2 pink text, #cf8ef4 lilac accent, Comfortaa + feather icons) and the pink/lilac selection colours in rofi config.rasi. Colours are inconsistent across apps, dunst has square corners, there are no shadows and no working blur, and the bar has no pills or islands. By 2026 standards it is dated and well below Hyprland/Quickshell rices such as end-4, JaKooLit or HyDE. I could not view the screenshots (images/screenshot.png is about 1.6MB), so this judgment comes from the config files.

components.compositor: X11: bspwm is the window manager, picom is the compositor (ibhagwan/sdhand fork keys: corner-radius, round-borders, kawase blur, experimental-backends), and sxhkd handles hotkeys.
components.bar_or_shell: Polybar ('bar/example', top, full width, wm-restack=bspwm, enable-ipc). Left: bspwm workspaces I–VII, MPRIS now-playing (Python dbus script with scrolling text and playerctl buttons), download/upload speed. Center: polywins (a clickable window-icon list that raises or hides windows). Right: pulseaudio, mic (script), backlight (amdgpu_bl1), redshift toggle/temperature, battery (BAT1), temperature, memory, bluetooth, wlan (wlp3s0), eth (enp2s0), time, and a custom/menu powermenu (reboot/poweroff via sudo systemctl, betterlockscreen, bspc quit).
components.launcher: rofi. sxhkd super+space runs `rofi -show drun -sidebar-mode -columns 3`, using legacy CLI flags (-lines, -width, -padding). config.rasi sets modi drun, window, filebrowser, run and a custom 'Kill' script. Script menus: appsmenu, backlight, keyboard-layout, kill, mpdmenu, powermenu (sidebar five.rasi, which launches promptmenu for confirmation), volume, wifi-menu. The themes are adapted from the 'rofi-menus'/'darker-than-black' collections (credited to Avasz/deadguy in the file header).
components.notifications: dunst: dark #20242d, square corners, frame 5px #9a9fa0, geometry '300x6-16+40', follows the mouse, Iosevka FT 9, markup full.
components.lock_idle_logout: betterlockscreen (dim_level 40, blur_level 1, lock_timeout 300, default white ring, wrong colour d23c3dff). Bound to alt+shift+x (`betterlockscreen -l dim`); the polybar menu uses `-l dimblur`. The rofi powermenu calls `lxlock` instead, which is inconsistent. There is no idle daemon (no xss-lock/xidlehook). Logout is `pkill -KILL -u $(whoami)` or `bspc quit`.
components.wallpaper_tool: nitrogen (--restore in bspwmrc). feh is used by betterlockscreen.
components.terminal: kitty: JetBrains Mono 11.7, background_opacity 0.9, Dracula, padding 10/20, tab bar at the top with powerline-ish fade templates (#afc3fb active), layouts horizontal/splits/grid/fat, shell zsh, split-management keymaps in mappings.conf.
components.shell_prompt: zsh with oh-my-zsh and powerlevel10k (.p10k.zsh is the stock wizard output: os_icon/dir/vcs/newline/prompt_char), plugins git, archlinux, zsh-syntax-highlighting and zsh-autosuggestions. .bashrc uses starship. A bare-repo alias `mydotfiles` manages the dotfiles.
components.editor: No editor config in the current tree. A Jan 2022 commit says 'added neovim' but no nvim directory exists at HEAD. There is an alias nv=nvim, and picom has rules for 'Code'.
components.file_manager: ranger (rc.conf plus scope.sh) and nautilus (search-metadata only).
components.fetch: neofetch with the stock-like config.conf (ascii backend, distro colours, colour blocks 0–15).
components.login_boot: No display manager and no bootloader or Plymouth theme. It starts through .xinitrc, which is broken: the stock twm/xclock/xterm lines, including `exec xterm ... -name login`, come before `exec dbus-launch ... bspwm`, so startx runs twm and xterm and bspwm never launches. It also hardcodes usermodmap=/home/arch/.Xmodmap.
components.extras: cava (ncurses, 8-colour pastel-rainbow gradient, bar_width 2, spacing 1) with GLSL shaders (bar_spectrum.frag, northern_lights.frag). Spicetify with the Dribbblish and Sleek themes and the extensions dribbblish, popuplyrics, fullappdisplay, webnowplaying and trashbin. mpd, ytmdl, bpytop/bashtop, redshift (polybar toggle with an env file), maim/xclip screenshots, unclutter, etc/pacman.conf (Color, ILoveCandy, ParallelDownloads = 10, DownloadUser = alpm).

standout_features: polybar-now-playing: a Python dbus/MPRIS script. It scrolls long titles in a fixed 20-char window (with east-asian-width handling), shows a per-player prefix icon (spotify/firefox/default), draws clickable playerctl prev/play-pause/next buttons with %{A:...:} tags, and cycles between players on SIGUSR1 (right-click). The same idea is easy to port to a Waybar custom module or a Quickshell MPRIS widget.

polywins.sh: a taskbar in the bar center that lists open windows as icons (`xprop -root -spy _NET_CLIENT_LIST _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW`). Clicking an active window hides it (`bspc node -g hidden=on`), clicking another focuses it, scrolling resizes it, and middle-click closes it. On Hyprland the equivalent is hyprland/taskbar or wlr/taskbar.

Rofi confirmation menu: powermenu.sh (vertical 5-icon sidebar using the feather icon font, anchored east at 6% width) calls a generic promptmenu.sh that takes --yes-command/--no-command/--query flags. This yes/no dialog can be reused for any destructive action.

Rofi theme system with a single switch file: sidebar/colors.rasi @imports one colorscheme, and shared/settings.rasi @imports a colorscheme plus a resolution file (1366x768 or 1920x1080). Swapping one import re-themes every menu.
Polybar redshift module: click to toggle, scroll to change temperature in 300K steps. State lives in env.sh and is rewritten with sed. The Wayland version would be hyprsunset or wlsunset.
cava GLSL shaders (northern_lights.frag) and a pastel 8-stop gradient (#80a0ff→#ff5189), which make a nice visualizer palette.
Spicetify Dribbblish (purple scheme) with the popuplyrics and fullappdisplay extensions, for a themed Spotify.
structure_install: A flat $HOME mirror managed as a bare git repo (alias `mydotfiles='/usr/bin/git --git-dir=$HOME/.my-dotfiles/ --work-tree=$HOME'`). Root: .Xmodmap, .Xresources, .bashrc, .zshrc, .p10k.zsh, .xinitrc, README.md, etc/pacman.conf, and images/ (2 screenshots plus 1 wallpaper). .config/ has bashtop, bpytop, betterlockscreenrc, bspwm, cava (plus shaders), dunst, kitty (plus 11 colour schemes), mpd, nautilus, neofetch, picom, polybar (plus 11 scripts), ranger, rofi (config, 9 scripts, themes/shared/{colorschemes,resolutions}, sidebar), spicetify (Backup .spa blobs, 5 extensions, 2 themes), sxhkd and ytmdl. There is no install script, no package list, no dependency docs and no NixOS/flake/home-manager support. The user has to clone it into $HOME by hand and install bspwm, sxhkd, polybar, the picom fork, rofi, dunst, kitty, nitrogen, betterlockscreen, redshift, playerctl, python-dbus, wmctrl, slop, maim, xclip, unclutter, oh-my-zsh, p10k and the fonts themselves.

key_snippets.purpose: Bug: the stock twm/xterm block runs `exec xterm` before bspwm, so bspwm never starts via startx
key_snippets.excerpt:
twm &
xclock -geometry 50x50-1+1 &
xterm -geometry 80x50+494+51 &
xterm -geometry 80x20+494-0 &
exec xterm -geometry 80x66+0+0 -name login
sxhkd &
exec dbus-launch --autolaunch=$(cat /var/lib/dbus/machine-id) bspwm

weaknesses: It is not a Hyprland or Wayland config at all. It runs on X11 with bspwm, sxhkd, polybar, the picom fork, nitrogen, xclip, maim, xprop, wmctrl, slop and xrandr, so none of it drops into Hyprland on Arch or NixOS without a rewrite.
No NixOS support: no flake, no home-manager, no modules and no package list.
No install script or dependency list. The README is only screenshots.
.xinitrc is broken: the leftover stock `twm &` and `exec xterm ... -name login` come before `exec ... bspwm`, so startx never reaches bspwm, and the lines after it never run.

Hardcoded usernames and paths that disagree with each other: /home/arch/.Xmodmap, /home/arch/.local/bin, /home/arch/Music (ytmdl), /home/saurabh/.spicetify, /home/saurabh/.config/spotify/prefs, /home/saurabh/callow/chromedriver. The shell configs also carry personal aliases (caa/sophos VPN, mysql).
Hardcoded hardware names: interface wlp3s0 and enp2s0, battery BAT1/AC0, backlight card amdgpu_bl1, thermal-zone 0, `xrandr --dpi 96`.

Outdated syntax. picom `experimental-backends = true` was removed in picom v10 and makes current picom error out. The corner-radius/round-borders/kawase blur keys come from the old ibhagwan/sdhand forks. dunst `geometry`/`shrink`/`notification_height` are deprecated and were replaced by width/height/offset in 1.7+. Rofi CLI flags `-lines -width -padding -location` were removed in rofi 1.7.
Nerd Fonts v2 codepoints (墳 ﬘ 祝 雷 ﭢ 喇 ﭠ) sit in the Material Design range that Nerd Fonts v3 removed, so they render as the wrong glyphs or tofu on current fonts.

Colours are inconsistent: Dracula in kitty, .Xresources and bspwm, Nord-grey #20242d in dunst and rofi, a cyan #63c5ea rofi accent, and polywins red/green. There is no single source of truth or generator.
Rofi bugs: config.rasi references the undefined variables @pink and @fg. powermenu locks with `lxlock` while everything else uses betterlockscreen.
Blur is set but disabled (background=false), shadows are off, and dunst has corner_radius 0. Kitty opacity 0.9 is stacked under a picom 60% rule for kitty, which makes text hard to read.
Polybar powermenu calls `sudo systemctl reboot/poweroff`, which needs a password or a sudoers hack. Logout uses `pkill -KILL -u $(whoami)`.

Redistribution problems: it bundles about 15.6MB of Spotify's proprietary client assets (.config/spicetify/Backup/xpui.spa about 11MB, login.spa about 4.6MB). The 3840x2160 wallpaper has no source credit or license. There is no repo LICENSE.
Clutter: kitty.conf.save, 11 unused kitty colour schemes, the complete stock p10k config, and a full .Xmodmap keycode dump.
No GTK/Qt/cursor/icon theming, no idle daemon, no display manager and no boot theming.
steal_list: Pastel palette tokens for a cute theme: #f9f9f9 base, #fa74b2 pink text, #cf8ef4 lilac accent, #ffb6c1 light pink, #b19cd9 light purple, #9370DB medium purple, #e75480 dark pink. Pair them with Dracula #bd93f9/#ff79c6 for active/focused Hyprland borders, e.g. `col.active_border = rgba(ff79c6ff) rgba(bd93f9ff) 45deg`.

Fonts: Comfortaa for rounded, friendly launcher and power-menu text plus a thin line-icon font (feather, or Lucide/Material Symbols Rounded today). JetBrains Mono or Iosevka Nerd Font (v3) for the terminal and bar.

Rebuild the MPRIS now-playing module on Wayland: scrolling title, per-player icon, clickable prev/play/next via playerctl. Use a Waybar custom module or a Quickshell/AGS Mpris service instead of Python dbus.
The generic confirmation-dialog pattern (promptmenu.sh with --yes-command/--query) in front of a vertical icon power menu anchored to a screen edge. Port it to rofi-wayland or fuzzel, or use wlogout.
Rofi theming with one colors.rasi @import switch, generated by matugen or wallust instead of edited by hand.
A night-light toggle in the bar (click to toggle, scroll to adjust ±300K). Implement it with hyprsunset on Hyprland; don't use sed state files.

A pastel cava gradient (#80a0ff #74b2ff #79dac8 #85dc85 #36c692 #f09479 #e2637f #ff5189), or better, generate cava colours from the wallpaper palette. Consider the northern_lights.frag shader for the cava OpenGL output.
Spicetify (Dribbblish or Comfy) themed from the same palette. On NixOS use the spicetify-nix flake. Never commit the xpui.spa backups.
pacman.conf niceties for the Arch side: Color, ILoveCandy, VerbosePkgLists, ParallelDownloads = 10.

Mistakes to avoid when writing the new configs: don't hardcode interface, battery or backlight names (Waybar and Quickshell can auto-detect them); don't hardcode /home/<user> (use $HOME, ~, or `config.home.homeDirectory` in home-manager); use Nerd Fonts v3 codepoints; ship a real installer and a flake.

one_line: A small, plain i3wm/X11 Arch setup managed with GNU Stow: polybar, picom, rofi, dunst, WezTerm/Alacritty, oh-my-zsh and Neovim. It has no Hyprland, no Wayland and no Nix, and uses several colour schemes that don't match. It isn't a cute or pastel rice, and it's only worth borrowing a few small ideas from.
freshness: Stale. The Atom feed at github.com/kamolmachine/dotfiles/commits.atom shows the last commit on 2024-04-20 ("docs: update readme"), after "feat: setup nvim" and "refactor(global): rm unused modules...". Commits go back to 2023-11-11 ("setup oh my fish"). There has been no activity for about 2.5 years as of 2026-09-25. The README's own Todo still says "Switch to Wayland and tools optimized for it", so that never happened. The README screenshot URL points to github.com/chupapee/dotfiles, which suggests the account was renamed. There is no LICENSE file in the tree.

aesthetic.palette: The palette is inconsistent: there is no single scheme. (1) Rofi dark is Catppuccin Mocha: bg #1e1e2e (also used for border and selection), blue accent #89b4fa, fg #cdd6f4, selected text #f38ba8, grey #6c7086. (2) Rofi light is Catppuccin Latte: bg #eff1f5, blue #1e66f5, fg #4c4f69, selected #d20f39, grey #9ca0b0. (3) Dunst is Catppuccin Frappé: bg #303446, fg #c6d0f5, frame #8caaee, critical frame #ef9f76. (4) Alacritty is Horizon Dark: bg #1c1e26, fg #e0e0e0; normal colours black #16161c, red #e95678, green #29d398, yellow #fab795, blue #26bbd9, magenta #ee64ac, cyan #59e1e3, white #d5d8da; bright colours black #5b5858, red #ec6a88, green #3fdaa4, yellow #fbc3a7, blue #3fc4de, magenta #f075b5, cyan #6be4e6. (5) WezTerm switches between built-in 'Horizon Dark (base16)' and 'Alabaster'. (6) Polybar keeps the stock example colours: background #cc000000, background-alt #444, foreground #dfdfdf, foreground-alt #555, primary #ffb52a, secondary #e60053, alert #bd2c40, line-color #f00. (7) Neovim uses tokyonight-night. (8) GTK toggles between Adwaita and Adwaita-dark.
aesthetic.color_pipeline: Colours are static and hand-written per app. There is no matugen, wallust, pywal or stylix, and no templates. The only dynamic behaviour is a dark/light toggle: wm/.config/i3/scripts/theme-switcher.sh (bound to $mod+m, alias `st`) reads `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme`, switches between Adwaita and Adwaita-dark, and runs `sed -i` on ~/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini. WezTerm follows the change on its 'window-config-reloaded' event by running gsettings and choosing Alabaster or Horizon Dark. Rofi has matching light and dark .rasi files, but config.rasi hardcodes `@theme "catppuccin-dark"` and the switcher never changes it. Polybar, dunst and Alacritty don't follow the toggle at all.
aesthetic.fonts: i3: `pango:Inconsolata Medium 11`. Polybar: `Fira Code Nerd Font:pixelsize=10;1` (font-0 and font-2), plus a size=8 non-antialiased variant as font-1. Rofi: `Fira Code 14`. Alacritty: Fira Code size 10, with Regular, Bold, Italic and Bold Italic set. WezTerm: `wezterm.font 'Fira Code'` at 12.0. Dunst: `Monospace 12`. The bar icons are Nerd Font glyphs (e.g. 󰂄 󰂂 󰁹 󱑇 󰇧 󰐥 󰝟).
aesthetic.icons_cursor_gtk_qt: Rofi uses icon-theme "papirus" with show-icons true. Dunst uses icon_theme Adwaita, with icon_path pointing at the legacy /usr/share/icons/gnome/16x16/status and devices folders. GTK is only Adwaita or Adwaita-dark, set through gsettings and gtk-3.0/settings.ini. There is no cursor theme, Qt/Kvantum setup, or GTK 4/libadwaita colour-scheme handling.
aesthetic.geometry: i3: `default_border pixel 0`, `default_floating_border pixel 0`, `gaps inner 10`, `gaps outer 1`, `smart_gaps on`, and `for_window [class="^.*"] border pixel 0`, so there are no window borders at all. Picom: corner-radius 5 (docks and desktop excluded); shadow on with shadow-radius 7 and offsets -7/-7 at the default 0.75 opacity; inactive-opacity 0.9; frame-opacity 0.7; fading on, but fade-in-step and fade-out-step are 1.0, which makes fades effectively instant. blur-kern is "3x3box", but blur-method and blur-background are commented out, so there is effectively no blur. Backend is "xrender" with vsync true. Wintypes: tooltip opacity 0.75, dropdown_menu 0.8, popup_menu 1. Polybar: bottom bar, height 15, border-size 8 (same colour as the bar, so it acts as padding), width 100%, wm margins 5, module-margin-left 1, autohidden by a script. Rofi: width 1200, window height 600px, border 3px in the same colour as the background, inputbar border-radius 5px, prompt pill radius 3px with 6px padding and margins of 20px, listview 3 columns × 5 lines (2 in the light theme), element padding 5px, icon size 25px, mode-switcher buttons padding 10px. Dunst: width 400, height 400, origin top-right, offset 10x10, frame_width 3, padding and horizontal_padding 12, corner_radius 0, separator_height 2, progress_bar_height 10 with width 150–300 and radius 0, min/max icon 32/128, notification_limit 4. Terminals: padding 8 on all sides, Alacritty opacity 1 and decorations none.
aesthetic.animations: There are essentially no animations. It's i3 on X11 with no animation support, and picom's fade-in-step and fade-out-step of 1.0 make fades instant. Picom v12's `animations` block isn't used. The only motion is WezTerm's cursor blink: cursor_blink_rate 700 with ease-in and ease-out both 'Constant', and default_cursor_style 'BlinkingBlock'. Alacritty's cursor is a blinking Block. Polybar's battery module has 750ms charging and discharging animation frames defined, but its format lines using them are commented out.
aesthetic.wallpapers: No wallpapers are bundled, which is good for licensing. The README credits "The last of us" wallpapers. At runtime, `shuf -e -n1 ~/wallpapers/* | xargs feh --bg-scale` runs on every i3 start or reload and on $mod+w. The lock screen uses `shuf -e -n1 ~/wallpapers/*.png | xargs i3lock -t -i`, so it needs PNGs in a hardcoded ~/wallpapers folder. There is no slideshow; the i3 config has a TODO for one. The only image in the repo is the screenshot assets/i3wm.png.
aesthetic.vibe: It's a functional, minimal, somewhat unfinished developer i3 setup. It is not cute, pastel or especially polished: borderless tiled windows, 10px gaps, 5px rounding, and a tiny 15px black bottom bar that autohides and still uses polybar's stock orange/pink example colours. It mixes Catppuccin Mocha, Frappé and Latte with Horizon Dark and Tokyo Night. The most attractive piece is the Catppuccin rofi launcher: a 3-column app grid with a blue pill prompt and pink selected text. Overall polish is low to moderate, a typical "my first i3 rice" rather than a showcase. For a top-tier cute Hyprland rice it gives little beyond a few small UX ideas.

components.compositor: i3wm (X11), i3 config v4 generated by i3-config-wizard and then edited, with picom as the compositor (xrender backend, vsync, shadows, 5px corners). There's no Hyprland, Sway or other Wayland compositor. The README Todo lists "Switch to Wayland" as not done.
components.bar_or_shell: Polybar, bar name `main-bar`, launched by launch.sh (killall + pgrep wait) with IPC enabled. Left: internal/i3 workspaces with icon labels (1: , 2: 󰅩, 3: ), focused workspace in #ffb52a. Centre: xwindow title truncated to 30 characters. Right: xkeyboard, pulseaudio, a custom brightnessctl script (icon ramp chosen from percentage thresholds), battery (BAT0/AC), date (%H:%M, alt %d.%m.%y and seconds), and powermenu. The bar sits at the bottom and is autohidden by polybar-visibility-toggler.sh. There's no quickshell, AGS or eww.
components.launcher: Rofi with modi drun and window, sidebar-mode, papirus icons and drun-display-format "{icon} {name}". Two custom themes, catppuccin-dark.rasi (Mocha) and catppuccin-light.rasi (Latte), with config.rasi hardcoded to dark. $mod+d runs `rofi -show drun`. The terminal setting is "wterm", which is probably a typo for wezterm.
components.notifications: dunst, started with `exec_always dunst -config ~/.config/dunst/dunstrc`. It's themed with Catppuccin Frappé colours, has a progress bar, stacks duplicates, and maps mouse buttons: left closes the current notification, middle runs its action and closes it, right closes all. The README wrongly lists mako.
components.lock_idle_logout: Lock: $mod+Shift+x runs i3lock -t -i with a random PNG from ~/wallpapers. There's no idle daemon (no xss-lock or xidlehook). Logout: the stock $mod+Shift+e i3-nagbar prompt. The polybar powermenu button calls ~/.config/rofi/applets/bin/powermenu.sh, which isn't in the repo ("TODO: add applets"), so it's broken.
components.wallpaper_tool: feh --bg-scale with a random pick via shuf from ~/wallpapers, on every i3 start or reload and on $mod+w.
components.terminal: WezTerm is the main terminal ($mod+Return runs wezterm-gui): Fira Code 12, no tab bar, 8px padding, a unix_domains multiplexer, Ctrl+Alt+Arrow to split panes and Alt+Arrow to move between them, Super+P for the command palette, and colours that follow the GTK dark/light setting. alacritty.toml (Horizon Dark, Fira Code 10) is also included as a fallback.
components.shell_prompt: zsh with oh-my-zsh and ZSH_THEME="eastwood". Plugins: git, zsh-autosuggestions, zsh-syntax-highlighting, sudo, history, web-search. zoxide is initialised, with alias e=z. There's a set of eza aliases with --icons (l, lt, la, lat, li, ...) and pacman aliases (i=sudo pacman -S, u=-Syy, uu=-Syu). There's no starship or oh-my-posh.
components.editor: Neovim with a custom lazy.nvim config (init.lua loads core.mappings, core.options and lazy-config). Plugin files: autopairs, blankline, bufferline, center, colorscheme (tokyonight-night active; darcula-solid kept but disabled), file-browser, flash, lsp, lualine (lualine_x emptied), mini-indentscope, noice (bottom_search, command_palette, long_message_to_split, inc_rename presets), oil, rainbow-brackets, surround, telescope, treesitter, ufo, vimBeGood, which-key, yanky. There's also a leftover lazyvim.json file.
components.file_manager: There's no GUI or TUI file manager. oil.nvim and a file-browser plugin inside Neovim cover file browsing; I didn't read file-browser.lua, so I don't know which plugin it uses.
components.fetch: None.
components.login_boot: None: no display manager, bootloader theme or plymouth.
components.extras: CopyQ clipboard manager ($mod+v, floating window resized to 600x600, no border). Screenshots with maim + xclip: Print copies the full screen to the clipboard, Shift+Print copies a selection, and $mod+Print saves to /home/$USER/Pictures/screenshots/$(date). Media keys use playerctl, volume uses pactl (±3%), brightness uses brightnessctl (5%). cbatticon handles battery warnings (-l 20 -r 10). A vendored third-party battery-popup.sh (R-J Ekker, 2016) is included but never started. setxkbmap sets us,ru layouts with an Alt+Shift toggle. Apps are pinned to workspaces: firefox or Chrome to 1, Code to 2, Telegram to 3. There's no cava, spicetify, Firefox theme or Discord theme.

standout_features: Dark/light mode on one key: theme-switcher.sh flips the GTK theme through gsettings, and .wezterm.lua picks it up on 'window-config-reloaded' by running `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme` and applying 'Alabaster' or 'Horizon Dark (base16)' through window:set_config_overrides. The idea is useful, but only WezTerm and GTK actually follow it.

Matching Catppuccin Mocha and Latte rofi themes: a 3-column × 5-line icon grid (Latte uses 2 columns), a blue 'pill' prompt (#89b4fa background with dark text, radius 3px), pink selected text (#f38ba8) instead of a highlight bar, and papirus icons at 25px.
A bottom polybar that autohides when the mouse leaves the bottom edge (polybar-visibility-toggler.sh uses xdotool with polybar-msg hide/show every 0.1s), so the desktop feels clean and fullscreen.
One random wallpaper folder feeds both the desktop (feh) and the lock screen (i3lock), so the lock screen varies too.

A GNU Stow layout with one package per role (bar/, compositor/, dmenu/, editor/, notification-daemon/, shell/, terminal/, wm/), each holding its own .config tree, so you can install per component with `stow bar` and so on.
A dunst setup with a progress bar (height 10, width 150–300), stack_duplicates, notification_limit 4, and a sensible mouse mapping (left closes, middle runs the action, right closes all).
The polybar brightness module picks a brightness icon from the current percentage and uses scroll-wheel up/down to change brightness.
structure_install: The repo is a flat GNU Stow layout. Top-level folders are Stow packages named by role: assets/ (screenshot), bar/.config/polybar/{config.ini, colors.ini, launch.sh, modules/*.ini, scripts/brightnessctl.sh}, compositor/.config/picom/picom.conf, dmenu/.config/rofi/{config.rasi, catppuccin-dark.rasi, catppuccin-light.rasi}, editor/.config/nvim/{init.lua, lua/core, lua/plugins/*.lua, lazy-lock.json}, notification-daemon/.config/dunst/dunstrc, shell/.zshrc, terminal/{.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml, .wezterm.lua}, and wm/.config/i3/{config, scripts/battery-popup.sh, polybar-visibility-toggler.sh, theme-switcher.sh}. The repo has 85 tree entries in total. There's no install script, package list, bootstrap or Makefile. The README only lists the tools, and install is implied by the commit \"implement stow symlinking for easier conf file management\": run `stow <pkg>` from the repo inside $HOME. Dependencies aren't documented, so you have to work them out from the configs. From the configs: i3-wm, polybar, picom, rofi, dunst, wezterm, alacritty, zsh + oh-my-zsh + zsh-autosuggestions + zsh-syntax-highlighting, zoxide, eza, copyq, feh, i3lock, maim, xclip, xdotool, xorg-xrandr, brightnessctl, playerctl, libpulse (pactl), cbatticon, papirus-icon-theme, ttf-fira-code, a Fira Code Nerd Font, ttf-inconsolata, neovim.

key_snippets.purpose: WezTerm switches colour scheme to follow the system dark/light (GTK) setting. This pattern is worth adapting.
key_snippets.excerpt:
function scheme_for_appearance(appearance)
  if appearance:find 'Light' then
    return 'Alabaster'
  else
    return 'Horizon Dark (base16)'
  end
end

function query_appearance_gnome()
  local success, stdout = wezterm.run_child_process {
    'gsettings',
    'get',
    'org.gnome.desktop.interface',
    'gtk-theme',
  }
  if stdout:find 'dark' then
    return 'Dark'
  end
  return 'Light'
end

wezterm.on('window-config-reloaded', function(window, pane)
  local overrides = window:get_config_overrides() or {}
  local appearance = query_appearance_gnome()
  local scheme = scheme_for_appearance(appearance)
  if overrides.color_scheme ~= scheme then
    overrides.color_scheme = scheme
    window:set_config_overrides(overrides)
  end
end)

key_snippets.purpose: The best-looking piece in the repo: a Catppuccin Mocha rofi grid with a pill-shaped prompt.
The bar autohide idea, and an example of what not to do: it polls every 0.1s, and i3 starts it with exec_always, so every i3 reload adds another loop.
key_snippets.excerpt:
#!/bin/bash

polybar_height=15

while true; do
  window_height=$(xrandr | grep -m1 -oP '\d{3,}x\d+' | cut -d 'x' -f 2)
  mouse_y=$(xdotool getmouselocation | grep -oP 'y:\K\d+' | cut -d ':' -f 2)
  distance_from_bottom=$((window_height - mouse_y))

  if [ "$distance_from_bottom" -ge "$polybar_height" ]; then
    polybar-msg cmd hide
  else
    polybar-msg cmd show
  fi

  sleep 0.1
done

key_snippets.purpose: The dark/light toggle, which only flips the GTK theme name (the old approach, without color-scheme).
key_snippets.excerpt:
theme=$(gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme)
theme=${theme//\'/}

if [ "$theme" = "Adwaita-dark" ]; then
  sed -i "s/Adwaita-dark/Adwaita/g" ~/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme 'Adwaita'
  echo "Light mode activated"
else
  sed -i "s/Adwaita/Adwaita-dark/g" ~/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme 'Adwaita-dark'
  echo "Darkness surrounds us"
fi
