pkgs/default.nix auto-discovers packages with scanPaths and callPackage, injecting colorscheme and myvars into quickshell; build-time substituteInPlace --replace-fail of @placeholders@ into QML and scripts
Global vars file (vars/default.nix) imported as myvars/specialArgs for username, paths, monitors, theme, wallpaper
sops-nix for secrets (rclone config), .sops.yaml, age keys from ssh via ssh-to-age
systemd user services declared in NixOS (wallpaper, wallpaper-updater) and HM (quickshell)
greetd + niri + quickshell greeter; custom PAM service declared via security.pam.services.dats-lock
HM programs.distrobox for an Arch container; custom mylib.file.substitute for templating shell/fish files
Cachix binary cache (datsfilipe-dotfiles.cachix.org); CI build and lib tests (run_lib_tests)
No stylix, no disko, no impermanence, no flake-parts

key_snippets.purpose: Derive a whole UI tonal ramp from two base colors (bg/fg) + accent
key_snippets.excerpt:
function mix(a: color, b: color, t: real): color {
    return Qt.rgba(a.r + (b.r - a.r) * t, a.g + (b.g - a.g) * t, a.b + (b.b - a.b) * t, a.a + (b.a - a.a) * t);
  }
...
  readonly property QtObject colors: QtObject {
    readonly property color base: root.term.background
    readonly property color panel: root.mix(root.term.background, root.term.foreground, 0.06)
    readonly property color layer1: root.mix(root.term.background, root.term.foreground, 0.11)
    readonly property color layer2: root.mix(root.term.background, root.term.foreground, 0.17)

    readonly property color hover: root.alpha(root.term.foreground, 0.08)
    readonly property color press: root.alpha(root.term.foreground, 0.14)

    readonly property color outline: root.mix(root.term.background, root.term.foreground, 0.24)
    readonly property color outlineStrong: root.mix(root.term.background, root.term.foreground, 0.45)

    readonly property color text: root.term.foreground
    readonly property color subtext: root.mix(root.term.foreground, root.term.background, 0.14)
    readonly property color faint: root.mix(root.term.foreground, root.term.background, 0.34)

    readonly property color accent: root.term.primary
    readonly property color accentDim: root.mix(root.term.primary, root.term.background, 0.45)

key_snippets.purpose: Blurred, dimmed wallpaper backdrop shared by the lock screen and greeter
key_snippets.excerpt:
Image {
    id: backdrop

    anchors.fill: parent
    source: root.wallpaper === "" ? "" : "file://" + root.wallpaper
    sourceSize.width: 480
    fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectCrop
    visible: false
    asynchronous: false
    cache: true
  }

  MultiEffect {
    anchors.fill: parent
    source: backdrop
    visible: backdrop.status === Image.Ready
    blurEnabled: true
    blur: 1
    blurMax: 32
    brightness: -0.4
    saturation: -0.3
  }

  Rectangle {
    anchors.fill: parent
    color: Appearance.alpha(Appearance.colors.base, backdrop.status === Image.Ready ? 0.5 : 1)
  }

key_snippets.purpose: Base panel: hard offset 'brutalist' shadow plus scale/opacity pop-in from a chosen origin
key_snippets.excerpt:
Rectangle {
  id: root

  property bool shown: true
  property bool outlined: true
  property bool elevated: true
  property int growFrom: Item.Center

  color: Appearance.colors.panel
  radius: Appearance.rounding.normal
  border.width: root.outlined ? Appearance.elevation.borderWidth : 0
  border.color: Appearance.colors.outline

  transformOrigin: root.growFrom
  scale: root.shown ? 1 : 0.96
  opacity: root.shown ? 1 : 0

  Rectangle {
    z: -1
    x: Appearance.elevation.offset
    y: Appearance.elevation.offset
    width: parent.width
    height: parent.height
    visible: root.elevated
    color: Appearance.colors.shadow
  }

  Behavior on scale {
    Anim {
      speed: root.shown ? "enter" : "exit"
    }
  }

weaknesses: It does not match the brief. There is no Hyprland config at all (niri is primary; i3/sway are legacy), and no Arch Linux support: Arch appears only as a distrobox dev container. Everything is NixOS/Home Manager-specific, including build-time substitution into QML.

Hardcoded identity and paths: username 'dtsf', dotfiles = "/home/${username}/.dotfiles", wallpaper "/home/dtsf/gdrive/walls/70.png", Mod+Return hardcodes a zellij session suffix 'dtsf', and binds hardcode alacritty/brave/work-browser.

Wallpaper 'apply' is fragile and heavy. It sed-rewrites vars/default.nix with the regex '^    wallpaper = .*' (depends on exact 4-space indent) and then runs 'sudo nixos-rebuild switch' in a terminal just to change the wallpaper. Theme changes also need a full rebuild because colors are baked in at build time.

Likely stale reference: pkgs/focus-mode/conf/focus-mode.sh calls 'wbar-autohide autohideOn/Off', but the Quickshell package only provides 'wbar' (= qs ipc call shell). No 'wbar-autohide' is defined in this repo (it could come from the external unix-scripts input; unverified). It also keeps state in /tmp/focus-mode-active.
No idle management (no swayidle/hypridle equivalent) found for the niri session, so there is no auto-lock or DPMS on idle.

Copyright/licensing concerns in bundled art: asuka.gif (Evangelion character) ships in the Quickshell package, and shimeji-ee mascot archives are in Git LFS (contents not inspected). The preview wallpaper is Evangelion fan art (kept on Google Drive, not in the repo). The repo LICENSE is MIT, which does not cover that art.

The 'catppuccin' theme is mislabeled: bg #111111 and primary #ab9df2 are not Catppuccin values. GTK uses catppuccin-mocha for every theme, which clashes with gruvbox/solarized palettes. Exporting GTK_THEME globally is discouraged for libadwaita apps.
The README is out of date: it mentions an astal addon and 'templates'/'scripts' dirs that don't match the tree, and says submodules use ssh URLs.

Aesthetic is not cute/pastel: rounding tokens are all 0 and the bar uses text-only labels ('pwr', 'msg', 'eth', '|<'). The Nerd Font is packaged but barely used for glyphs. Shell corners are square (0) while niri windows are rounded (6).
Personal and unrelated cruft mixed into shared vars (Ollama persona system prompts, blocked hosts, pritunl VPN, work browser). Borrowing it takes pruning.
The launcher calculator uses Function('return (...)') eval, guarded only by a character regex. It is fine for a local user, but a real math parser would be cleaner.
steal_list: Adopt the Appearance.qml singleton pattern: define only bg/fg/accent (plus ANSI colors) and derive panel/layer1/layer2/outline/subtext/faint with mix(). For a pastel rice, feed it matugen output instead of static Nix attrs so it works identically on Arch and NixOS.

Copy the motion tokens: fast 200ms [0.34,0.80,0.34,1], std 350ms [0.42,1.67,0.21,0.90] (bouncy overshoot, great for cute), slow 500ms [0.38,1.21,0.22,1], enter 400ms [0.05,0.7,0.1,1], exit 200ms [0.3,0,0.8,0.15]. Translate the same curves into Hyprland 'bezier =' lines so compositor and shell motion match.

Card component with scale 0.96->1 and opacity pop from a per-popout transformOrigin (Top for launcher, TopRight for toasts). Swap the hard brutalist shadow for a soft pastel glow and set rounding to 12-16 for the cute look.

Expose every shell action as a named wrapper binary (wlauncher, wlock, wvolume-osd, wbar ...). On Arch these can be tiny shell scripts calling 'qs ipc call ...', and Hyprland binds stay distro-agnostic.

Shared AuthFace for both the lock screen (WlSessionLock + Quickshell PAM with a dedicated pam service) and the greetd greeter: blurred downsampled wallpaper (blurMax 32, brightness -0.4), per-char pop-in dots, shake on failure, now-playing caption.
Bottom MediaDock that animates exclusiveZone with reveal, with cava bars behind a scrim and a seek strip. Only subscribe to cava when visible and playing, to save CPU.
Bar autohide with a 4px reveal strip, a 700ms timer and a Region mask swap, plus a 'focus mode' toggle that hides the bar and wallpaper.
Launcher prefix modes: '>' run, '?' web search, '=' calculator. Add emoji/clipboard modes for extra delight.

Wallpaper picker with hover-to-preview on the live desktop and a cached ImageMagick thumbnail pipeline (420x260, parallel). Replace the rebuild-to-apply step with swww transitions + matugen regeneration + 'hyprctl reload' / Quickshell hot reload.
Multi-monitor spanning wallpaper cropping with a layout signature + md5 cache (useful for ultrawide or dual setups).
Close popouts automatically on focused-window or workspace change, driven by a compositor event-stream singleton (port the Niri.qml parser to Hyprland's socket2 or Quickshell.Hyprland).
Cute layer: an animated mascot GIF above the session menu and wl-shimeji desktop pets on a keybind. Use freely licensed or original mascot art to avoid copyright issues.
Color-picker-to-clipboard keybind (niri 'pick-color'; hyprpicker -a on Hyprland).
For the Nix side: the vertical-slice os.nix/user.nix layout with recursive scanPaths auto-import, per-app theme integration toggles, and a justfile 'fmt' target that includes qmlformat and kdlfmt.

one_line: A NixOS + Home Manager flake built on the author's own Denix framework. Its "rices" are an inheritable module layer (rounded "marui" vs square "shikakui"). A Nix-native base24 palette is templated into Hyprland, kitty, rofi, hyprlock, GTK/libadwaita, fcitx5, LibreWolf, Spicetify and VSCodium, with rotating anime wallpapers from a separate flake. The architecture is excellent, but the current tree has no bar or notification daemon and uses warm-dark earthy palettes rather than pastel ones.
freshness: Active but uneven. The newest commit on master is Jul 19, 2026 ("modules/programs/telegram: replace blatant spyware client..."). Earlier commits: Mar 30-31, 2026 (kdeconnect init, qt theme rename to adwaita, git new syntax), Dec 12, 2025 (radicale), and a Nov 30, 2025 batch fixing the pkgs.system deprecation warning. The committed flake.lock is stale: its newest input lastModified is 2025-08-12 (nixpkgs master about 2025-08-09). nixpkgs and home-manager track `master`. The README is out of date: it lists rices "Hito" and "Yami" (coffee / kanagawa-dragon) that no longer exist; the tree has marukutekurai and shikakukutekurai using biscuit-sol-dark. The README also says "Display Manager: -" even though modules/services/gdm.nix enables GDM for GUI hosts.

aesthetic.color_pipeline:
Static and Nix-native. There is no stylix, matugen, wallust or pywal.
- modules/config/colorschemes/default.nix defines a `colorscheme` submodule. It has `polarity` (dark|light), base00-base0F, and base10-base17 defaulted per the base24 styling fallbacks (base10/11 -> base00, base12 -> base08, base13 -> base0A, base14 -> base0B, base15 -> base0C, base16 -> base0D, base17 -> base0E).
- Each color string is passed through `ylib.color` from the author's nypkgs, which exposes `.hex`, `.rgb` and `.value`.
- The chosen scheme is exported as a shared module arg (`args.shared.colorscheme`), so every module receives `colorscheme`. A rice picks the scheme, e.g. `colorscheme = myconfig.colorschemes.biscuit-sol-dark`.

Consumers, each templated by hand:
- Hyprland: via the rice. background = rgb(base11), inactive border = rgba(base02 ee), active border = rgba(base03 ff).
- kitty: a full 16-color map following the base24-kitty template.
- rofi: selected/active = base0B, urgent = base08.
- hyprlock.
- GTK3/GTK4: a gtk.css file of libadwaita @define-color overrides.
- fcitx5: a generated theme.conf.
- LibreWolf: a theme XPI built with mkDerivation.
- Spicetify: the Text theme with customColorScheme.
- VSCodium: `ylib.vscodeBase24Theme`, a generated extension.
- Cursor and GTK/Qt theme variants flip on `polarity`.

Nothing is derived from the wallpaper.
aesthetic.fonts:
- modules/toplevel/fonts.nix installs noto-fonts, noto-fonts-cjk-serif, noto-fonts-cjk-sans, font-awesome and material-design-icons.
- Rofi: font "Noto Sans CJK JP 15px"; prompt and mode buttons use "Material Design Icons 20px" (glyphs 󱭼 drun, 󰃬 calc, 󰍉 search).
- fcitx5 theme: "Sans 13" for the panel, "Sans 10" for the menu.
- VSCodium: editor.fontFamily "'Droid Sans Mono', 'monospace', 'CaskaydiaCove Nerd Font'". No Nerd Font is installed by fonts.nix.
- Kitty: no font is set, so it uses kitty's default.
- The screenshot shows a monospace UI font and Japanese glyphs.
aesthetic.icons_cursor_gtk_qt:
- Cursor: Bibata-Modern-Ice when polarity is dark, Bibata-Modern-Classic when light (pkgs.bibata-cursors), size 24, with home.pointerCursor gtk.enable and hyprcursor.enable.
- GTK theme: adw-gtk3-dark (pkgs.adw-gtk3), with custom gtk-3.0/gtk-4.0 gtk.css libadwaita color overrides from the palette. The file ends with the hack `NautilusWindow * { }; // BLACKMAGIC without this, the style does not work in many programs`.
- Icon theme: Adwaita (adwaita-icon-theme).
- Qt: platformTheme.name "adwaita", style "adwaita-dark".
- VSCodium: workbench.iconTheme "bearded-icons".
aesthetic.geometry:
Hyprland module defaults (modules/programs/hyprland/default.nix):
- gaps_in 5, gaps_out 20
- border_size 1, rounding 0
- shadow enabled: range 10, render_power 4, offset "0 0", scale 1.0, color 0xff151010

Rice "marui" (rounded; used by marukutekurai on the mitama laptop):
- gaps inner 6, outer 12
- border size 2, rounding 6

Rice "shikakui" (square; used by shikakukutekurai on the jakuzure desktop):
- gaps 6/12, border size 0, rounding 0

Other Hyprland settings:
- snap enabled: window_gap 10, monitor_gap 10, border_overlap true
- Blur is not configured anywhere (Hyprland defaults apply), and there is a rule `noblur, class:Rofi`.
- No opacity or inactive-opacity settings.

Rofi:
- window width 600px, border 1.5px solid base0B, border-radius 10px
- mainbox padding 10px, spacing 10px
- inputbar is a pill split into prompt (radius 10px 0 0 10px) and entry (radius 0 10px 10px 0)
- elements have radius 10px and padding 5px 10px; listview has 8 lines, spacing 7.5px
- scrollbar handle 5px

Hyprlock:
- input-field 200x50, rounding 0, outline_thickness 0, dots_rounding 0
- background is flat base01

fcitx5: panel BorderWidth 2, text margins 10/10/6/6.
aesthetic.animations: Hyprland has none: there is no `animations`, `bezier` or `animation` key in settings.nix or the rice files, so compositor defaults apply. Hyprlock sets `animation = "fadeIn,0,0,default"`, which disables its fade. The only motion flourish is kitty's `cursor_trail = 3` with `cursor_trail_decay = "0.1 0.4"`.
aesthetic.wallpapers:
Wallpapers come from a separate flake input, github:yunfachi/nix-config-wallpapers: 137 images, each tagged (for example `akima, blue, night, city, girl`), with a README preview generated automatically.
- Credits: Pixiv artists 焦茶 (jiao_cha), あきま (akima), いちご飴 (ichigoame) and トーコ (touko), plus Wallhaven (including Girls' Last Tour fan art).
- No license for the images is stated.
- modules/config/wallpapers.nix filters out `excludedTags`, then builds a linkFarm `imagesDir`.
- The author's own wallpaper-manager (github:yunfachi/wallpaper-manager) runs as a systemd user service bound to the wallpaper daemon: swww by default on desktops, hyprpaper as an option. It rotates every 300000 ms (5 min).
- The README screenshot uses a jiao_cha-style painting: a sailor-uniform schoolgirl sitting on a pier with seagulls, one standing on her head.
aesthetic.vibe:
Cozy and understated, with a warm-dark "coffee shop" or earthy look. The README screenshot is genuinely polished and cohesive:
- a thin top bar with small pill workspace dots at the left, and a centered "11:43 - Tue 29" clock next to a now-playing song title (幽霊船戦 - 宝鐘マリン)
- floating/tiled windows with small rounding and thin muted borders
- a Vim-style editor, LibreWolf on monkeytype, and Spotify with the Spicetify Text theme and a pink particle visualizer
- all of it laid over soft anime illustration

Most of the cuteness comes from the wallpapers and the NixOwOS rebrand; the palettes themselves are desaturated browns and dusty accents. For a pastel/cute target it is only moderately cute. I'd rate it 6/10 on cuteness, 7.5/10 on polish, and 9/10 on Nix engineering.

The bar in the screenshot does not exist in the current tree, which has no bar module. So a checkout today would look barer than the screenshot.

components.compositor:
Hyprland, configured through Home Manager `wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings`, with NixOS `programs.hyprland.enable = true`.
- Plugin: hyprsplit (num_workspaces 10, persistent_workspaces true), which gives per-monitor workspaces through split:workspace / split:movetoworkspacesilent binds.
- Also uses split:swapactiveworkspaces (only when exactly 2 displays) and split:grabroguewindows.
- Input: kb_layout "us,ru", grp:win_space_toggle, natural_scroll.
- Gesture: "3, horizontal, workspace".
- Swallowing: enable_swallow with swallow_regex ^(kitty)$ and exception ^(noswallow)$.
- ecosystem: no_update_news and no_donation_nag are on.
- misc: disable_hyprland_logo, focus_on_activate, new_window_takes_over_fullscreen = 1.
components.bar_or_shell: None in the current tree: no waybar, ags, eww or quickshell module exists. `quickshell` (git+https://git.outfoxxed.me/quickshell/quickshell) is declared as a flake input but nothing references it. The README screenshot shows an older top bar (workspace dots, clock, now-playing); its source could not be found in the tree.
components.launcher: rofi with the rofi-calc plugin (modes drun and calc) and a custom 600px rounded theme built with homeconfig.lib.formats.rasi mkLiteral. It is bound to `$mod, a` as `rofi -modi "drun,calc" -show drun -show-icons -sidebar-mode`. rofi-rbw-wayland (Bitwarden via rbw) is bound to `$mod SHIFT, p` with `--action copy`.
components.notifications: None found: no swaync, mako or dunst module exists in the tree.
components.lock_idle_logout:
- hyprlock: flat base01 background, 200x50 square input field, "Password:" placeholder, "Wrong" fail text, grace 0, hide_cursor, no clock or image widgets. Bound to `$mod, l`.
- hypridle: lock_cmd `pidof hyprlock || hyprlock`, before_sleep_cmd `loginctl lock-session`. Locks at 25 min and runs `hyprctl dispatch dpms off` at 30 min.
- Logout: only `CTRLALT, Delete, exit`. There is no wlogout or power menu.
components.wallpaper_tool: swww (the default on desktops, run as a custom systemd user service `swww-daemon`) or hyprpaper (splash = false), driven by yunfachi/wallpaper-manager. That manager is a systemd service `ExecStart = ... start --dir <imagesDir> --interval 300000 --wallpaper-daemon swww` with BindsTo/PartOf set to the daemon's service.
components.terminal: kitty with base24 colors from the palette, cursor_trail 3, cursor_trail_decay "0.1 0.4", tab_bar_edge top, scrollback_lines 10000, enable_audio_bell false and confirm_os_window_close 0. `$mod SHIFT, Return` launches `kitty --title noswallow`, which bypasses swallowing.
components.shell_prompt: bash with starship. The format is $username $hostname $battery $nix_shell $directory $git_branch $cmd_duration $character, which reads as prose ("user at host in dir on branch took Xs"). Styles are all "bold dimmed green", the character is ❯ (red on error), git_branch ignores master/main, and nix_shell is bold purple. NixOS-level promptInit is also set for bash, fish and zsh, falling back to the HM starship.toml.
components.editor: VSCodium module (modules/programs/codium) with a generated `nypkgs-base24` color theme, bearded-icons, the activity bar hidden, minimap off, sticky scroll on, and vscord Discord RPC (idle text "idle ( ´ ▿ ` )"). The screenshot shows a Vim-style modal editor with a file tree. nixvim appears in flake.lock (probably as a transitive dependency), but no nixvim module exists in the tree.
components.file_manager: Nautilus, built as a buildEnv with nautilus-python, nautilus-open-any-terminal (set to kitty via dconf) and sushi previewer, with NAUTILUS_4_EXTENSION_DIR set. There is a float rule for org.gnome.NautilusPreviewer. Also GThumb (images) and Totem (video).
components.fetch: No fetch module found. The NixOwOS input (github:yunfachi/NixOwOS, enabled for both NixOS and HM) rebrands NixOS as "NixOwOS" with new logos and distro name; its README shows a fastfetch screenshot.
components.login_boot:
- Display manager: GDM (services.displayManager.gdm.enable for GUI hosts), which contradicts the README's "-".
- Boot loader: systemd-boot on UEFI (consoleMode "max", configurationLimit 10) or GRUB on legacy (nodev, efiSupport), with loader timeout 0.
- Plymouth on desktops: theme "breeze", logo nix-snowflake-white.png.
- Silent boot: consoleLogLevel 0, initrd.verbose false, kernelParams quiet, splash, rd.systemd.show_status=false, rd.udev.log_level=3, udev.log_priority=3.
- Per-display `video=NAME:WxH@R` kernel params are generated from host.displays.
components.extras:
- Spicetify (Gerg-L/spicetify-nix): Text theme with a custom palette mapping, snippets hideFriendActivityButton, hideFullScreenButton and roundedImages, custom CSS for circular avatars and player controls at 0.4 opacity, and devtools enabled.
- LibreWolf with a generated color-theme XPI (xpinstall.signatures.required = 0).
- Discord PTB with OpenASAR and Vencord.
- fcitx5 with mozc (Japanese) and a palette-generated theme with arrow.png and radio.png assets.
- hyprshot: output/active on `$mod s`; region with --freeze on `$mod SHIFT s`.
- wl-clipboard and wl-clip-persist (restarted on Hyprland reload).
- brightnessctl on `$mod` plus scroll; wpctl volume with a 1.5 limit.
- An xdotool random-delay autoclicker on mouse buttons 276 and 275.
- anime-game launchers (aagl), Steam, Heroic, Prism/Lunar Minecraft, OBS, Krita, Obsidian, Anki, Feishin, beets and qbittorrent.
- A `hacking` devShell (nmap, findomain, assetfinder, dirsearch, binwalk, foremost).

standout_features: Rices as a first-class Denix layer with inheritance: `delib.rice { name = "marui"; inheritanceOnly = true; }` holds only geometry (rounded, border 2, radius 6). `marukutekurai` then `inherits = ["marui"]` and adds the colorscheme. The square variant `shikakui` sets border 0 and radius 0. Each host sets `rice = "..."`, and switching happens through `nixos-rebuild switch` (README: "Multiple rices, switchable via nixos-rebuild switch and working across all hosts").

A typed base24 colorscheme option with spec-compliant fallbacks (base10-17 default to base00/08/0A/0B/0C/0D/0E). Colors are coerced into an object with `.hex`, `.rgb` and `.value`, so templates can write `rgba(${base02.value}ee)`, `rgb(${base01.rgb})` or `#${base05.hex}` without string munging.

A LibreWolf/Firefox theme generated as a real extension: a manifest.json with about 30 `theme.colors` keys from the palette, zipped into an XPI in a mkDerivation, with an addonId and install path under share/mozilla/extensions.

A generated libadwaita @define-color override written to both gtk-3.0/gtk.css and gtk-4.0/gtk.css (accent/destructive/success/warning/window/view/headerbar/sidebar/card/dialog/popover, plus the blue_1-5 … dark_1-5 ramps mapped from base16). This themes GTK4 and libadwaita apps without a GTK theme package.

A tagged wallpaper catalog as its own flake: 137 images with tags and an auto-updated README preview table. `excludedTags` filters it, and a systemd `wallpaper-manager` service that BindsTo swww.service or hyprpaper.service rotates wallpapers every 5 minutes.

A single `host.displays` list (name, primary, refreshRate, width, height, x, y) generates Hyprland `monitor=` lines, kernel `video=` params, and a conditional dual-monitor `split:swapactiveworkspaces` bind.

A `commands.windowManager.onStartup/onReload` abstraction: any module can append shell snippets, and each one is wrapped in pkgs.writeShellScript and becomes exec-once/exec. For example, wl-clip-persist re-execs itself under a unique process name so it can be pkill'ed on reload.
A palette-generated fcitx5 input-method theme (theme.conf plus PNG assets), which is rare in rices and useful for CJK users.

Host `features` (cli, gui, gaming, hacking, powersave, wireless) with defaultByHostType. Modules default their enable flags from `host.guiFeatured` or `host.cliFeatured`, so servers get no GUI automatically.
One flake emits both `nixosConfigurations` and standalone `homeConfigurations` (`mkConfigurations "home"`) from the same modules. This is the pattern that would let HM-only parts run on Arch.
structure_install:
Layout:
- flake.nix calls `denix.lib.configurations` with `paths = [./hosts ./modules ./rices]`; every .nix file is auto-imported (umport-style).
- hosts/: dekomori (server), jakuzure (desktop, DP-3 144Hz plus HDMI-A-1, rice shikakukutekurai, disko/ZFS/impermanence, immich, navidrome), mitama (laptop, eDP-1 60Hz, rice marukutekurai). Each host has default.nix, hardware.nix, shared.nix (settings exported to other hosts, such as wireguard IPs and ssh keys) and secrets.json.
- modules/config: colorschemes, commands, constants, hosts, persist, wallpapers.
- modules/programs: about 50 apps; Hyprland is split into default, settings, binds, rules and scripts/clicker.
- modules/services: hypridle, hyprpaper, swww, wallpaper-manager, pipewire, wireguard, xray, and others.
- modules/toplevel: boot, cursor, fonts, gtk, qt, disko, secrets, user, home-manager, xdg, nixowos.
- modules/infras: changelog and deshiro bots with databases.
- rices/ is described under standout_features.

Install: there is no install script and the README gives no install steps. It is the standard flake workflow: `nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#<host>`, or `home-manager switch --flake .#<name>` for the HM output.
- Home Manager runs as a NixOS module (useGlobalPkgs, useUserPackages, backupFileExtension \"home_manager_backup\").
- homeManagerUser is hardcoded to \"yunfachi\".
- Secrets use sops-nix (.sops.yaml plus per-host secrets.json, decryptSecret / decryptHostSecretFile helpers).
nix_patterns: Denix framework (github:yunfachi/denix): `delib.module { name; options; myconfig.ifEnabled; nixos.ifEnabled; home.ifEnabled; }`. NixOS, Home Manager and custom options live in one file; `singleEnableOption host.guiFeatured` gives feature-driven defaults.
`delib.host` and `delib.rice` abstractions: rices support `inherits` and `inheritanceOnly`, and hosts choose a rice, a type (desktop/server) and features.

Denix extensions: `args` (shared module args such as colorscheme, constants, homeconfig and spicetifyPkgs) and `base.withConfig` host features (cli, gui, gaming, hacking, powersave, wireless) with defaultByHostType.
Dual output from one tree: nixosConfigurations = mkConfigurations "nixos" and homeConfigurations = mkConfigurations "home", selected via `moduleSystem`.
Home Manager as a NixOS module, plus a `homeconfig` arg that resolves to `config` or `config.home-manager.users.<user>`, so NixOS modules can read HM paths.
sops-nix secrets with per-host and shared secrets.json; the wireguard mesh between all hosts is declared in each host's shared.nix.
disko + impermanence (persist.user.directories are declared inside each app module, e.g. discord, spotify, nautilus thumbnails) + ZFS on jakuzure.
Custom library flake nypkgs (`ylib.color`, `ylib.vscodeBase24Theme`) injected via `_module.args`.
Third-party flakes: spicetify-nix, aagl-gtk-on-nix, nix-vscode-extensions, quickshell (unused), burpsuitepro, NixOwOS, wallpaper-manager, nix-config-wallpapers.
nixpkgs and home-manager pinned to `master` branches, not nixos-unstable.
Impure evaluation: boot.mode defaults via `builtins.pathExists /sys/firmware/efi/efivars`.

key_snippets.purpose: The rice layer: palette-driven Hyprland geometry for the rounded variant
base24 option schema with spec fallbacks; colors coerced via ylib.color
Palette to libadwaita color override for GTK3 and GTK4
Wallpaper rotation service bound to whichever daemon (swww/hyprpaper) is active
Monitors generated from host.displays and the startup/reload command abstraction; also shows old syntax (new_window_takes_over_fullscreen)
Apparent syntax error at HEAD: two extra closing braces (brace count 11 open vs 13 close)

weaknesses: The desktop shell is incomplete in the current tree: no bar, notification daemon, OSD, logout/power menu or clipboard-history UI. `quickshell` is a flake input that nothing uses. The bar in the README screenshot has no source in the tree.

hosts/jakuzure/default.nix appears to be a Nix parse error at HEAD: 11 `{` vs 13 `}`, with two stray `};` lines at the end. Denix imports every file under ./hosts, so this would likely break evaluation of every configuration. I found this by counting braces; I did not run nix eval.

Hyprland syntax is outdated for current releases. It uses `windowrulev2` with v1-style rule names (`noblur, class:Rofi`, `pseudo, class:fcitx`, `float, class:...`) and `misc:new_window_takes_over_fullscreen`. The Hyprland v0.53.0 release notes say "Windowrule syntax has been completely overhauled" and "`misc:on_focus_under_fullscreen` replaces `misc:new_window_takes_over_fullscreen`". The Hyprland wiki also now states "Since Hyprland 0.55, hyprlang is deprecated in favor of lua", so an HM `settings` attrset approach will need migration.
The flake.lock is stale: its newest input is 2025-08-12, while commits continue into 2026. Tracking nixpkgs and home-manager `master` rather than nixos-unstable adds breakage risk.

The README is stale and inconsistent: it names rices Hito, Marui and Yami, but the tree has marukutekurai, shikakukutekurai, marui and shikakui. It says there is no display manager, but gdm.nix enables GDM.

Hardcoded identity and locale: constants.nix sets username "yunfachi", fullname "Yun Fachi" and email yunfachi@gmail.com, flake homeManagerUser = "yunfachi", kb_layout "us,ru", and swallow_regex is tied to kitty with a FIXME. The module name has a typo, "coloschemes".
No animations, bezier curves, blur tuning or opacity are configured, so it relies on compositor defaults. hyprlock is bare (no clock, avatar or blurred screenshot). There is little motion polish.
The palettes are all dark and earthy or desaturated (biscuit-sol-dark, coffee, kanagawa-dragon, paradise). There is nothing pastel or light, so the cute factor comes almost entirely from wallpapers.
Wallpaper licensing risk: 137 Pixiv and Wallhaven artworks (焦茶, あきま, いちご飴, トーコ, Girls' Last Tour fan art) are redistributed in a public repo with credits but no stated license or permission.

Fragile hacks: the xdotool autoclicker is X11-only and runs under XWayland, it keeps state in /tmp/clicker.data, and it loops with a random delay; it also looks like a game-bot helper. The GTK `NautilusWindow * { };` 'BLACKMAGIC' hack. The fcitx toggle bind is written in bashisms. Boot mode uses an impure `builtins.pathExists /sys/firmware/efi/efivars`.
Fonts are thin: no Nerd Font is installed, even though VSCodium references 'CaskaydiaCove Nerd Font', and kitty has no font set.

Questionable inputs: `github:xiv3r/Burpsuite-Professional` is a third-party repackaging of a commercial product with unclear licensing. OpenASAR and Vencord client mods for Discord violate Discord's ToS.

Porting to Arch is hard: it is NixOS-first and depends on Denix plus the author's personal libraries (nypkgs, wallpaper-manager). The standalone homeConfigurations output exists, but its GUI modules assume the NixOS Hyprland module, GDM and sops.
steal_list: Adopt the rice-inheritance pattern: separate a geometry-only base rice (rounded or square: border, radius, gaps) from a palette rice that inherits it. Hosts then pick a rice name, and one switch changes the whole look.

Copy the typed base24 colorscheme option with spec fallbacks, plus a color type exposing `.hex`, `.rgb` and `.value`. Add pastel light and dark schemes (for example Rosé Pine Dawn or Catppuccin Latte/Mocha as base24) alongside it.

Generate libadwaita `@define-color` overrides into both gtk-3.0 and gtk-4.0 gtk.css from the palette, on top of adw-gtk3. On Arch, render the same CSS from the same template via a tiny generator script.
Generate a Firefox/LibreWolf theme XPI from the palette (manifest.json `theme.colors`, zipped into a mkDerivation) for a browser that matches the rice with no manual steps.
Map the palette into Spicetify with the Text theme via customColorScheme, plus the roundedImages snippet and small CSS snippets (circular avatars, dimmed controls at opacity 0.4).

Keep wallpapers as a separate tagged catalog with `excludedTags`, rotated by a systemd user service that `BindsTo` the wallpaper daemon (swww, now awww, or hyprpaper). Only include wallpapers with clear licenses or permission.
Declare displays once in a single host list and generate Hyprland monitor lines, kernel `video=` params and multi-monitor binds from it.

Use a startup/reload command registry that any module can append to, with each snippet wrapped as a script for exec-once/exec, and a pkill plus `exec -a <unique-name>` pattern for reload-safe daemons.
Kitty `cursor_trail 3` with `cursor_trail_decay "0.1 0.4"`, a cheap and cute motion touch. Also kitty swallowing with a `--title noswallow` escape hatch.

Reuse the rofi theme structure (600px, radius 10px, pill inputbar split into prompt and entry, Material Design Icons glyph prompts, rofi-calc mode) and recolor it pastel. Consider fuzzel or quickshell for the Wayland-native path.
hypridle listeners: lock at 25 min, dpms off at 30 min, before_sleep_cmd `loginctl lock-session`, and lock_cmd `pidof hyprlock || hyprlock`.

Silent boot recipe: systemd-boot with timeout 0 and consoleMode max, Plymouth, consoleLogLevel 0, and `quiet splash rd.systemd.show_status=false rd.udev.log_level=3 udev.log_priority=3`. Swap Plymouth breeze for a cute theme.

Hyprland niceties: `general.snap` (window_gap 10, monitor_gap 10, border_overlap), `ecosystem.no_update_news` and `no_donation_nag`, and hyprsplit for per-monitor workspaces. Rewrite window rules to the 0.53+ syntax and plan for the 0.55 Lua config.
Bibata-Modern-Ice cursor at size 24 with hyprcursor enabled, flipped to Classic by palette polarity.
Palette-generated fcitx5 theme for CJK input users.
Feature flags per host type (cli, gui, gaming, powersave, wireless), with module enable flags defaulting from them.
Emit both nixosConfigurations and standalone homeConfigurations from the same module tree, so the Arch path can use Home Manager standalone for user-level theming.

one_line: A tidy, NixOS-only flake for Qtile on X11. It uses a custom deep-navy and periwinkle palette inspired by Catppuccin, plus catppuccin/nix, picom, dunst, kitty and betterlockscreen. It has no Hyprland or Wayland content at all. Its best idea is a NixOS VM test that boots the real config and takes the README screenshot automatically in CI.
freshness: Actively maintained. Per the commits Atom feed, the last commits were on 2026-09-14 ("Update screenshot" from the CI bot and "~/nvim: add qmlls lsp"). Other commits landed in Aug, Jul and May 2026, including "~/nvim: update to 0.12" and "flake: update lockfile". The flake pins nixos-unstable, nixos-25.11 (stable) and catppuccin/nix ref v26.05, and flake.lock lastModified values reach about Aug 2026. Qtile is pinned to a separate nixpkgs commit (83b8ff5a…) as "nixpkgs-qtile-0-36". The README is badly out of date: it lists the Xanmod kernel, Bpytop, Ranger, Sublime and JetBrains, and "cp -r .* ~ / --recurse-submodules". None of that matches the Nix code, which uses linuxPackages_latest, btop, and has no submodules. .gitattributes still points to config/bpytop and config/neofetch paths that no longer exist. License: GPLv3.

aesthetic.palette: A custom palette the README calls 'inspired from Catppuccin Mocha', with deeper, more saturated bases. Source of truth: home/qtile/src/colors.py. BG_DARK #0F0F1C, BG_LIGHT #1A1C31, BG_LIGHTER #22263F; RED #D22942/#DE4259; GREEN #17B67C/#3FD7A0; YELLOW #F2A174/#EED49F; BLUE_VERY_DARK #3F3D9E, BLUE (main accent, periwinkle) #8B8AF1/#A7A5FB; PURPLE #D78AF1/#E5A5FB; CYAN #8ADEF1/#A5EBFB; TEXT_INACTIVE #292C39, TEXT_DARK #A2B1E8, TEXT_LIGHT #CAD3F5. The same palette is copied by hand into several places and has drifted. The README table lists cyan 4FCFEB/82E3F8, yellow-light EEC09F and white B4C0EC. Kitty's color4 is #8C8AF1 rather than #8B8AF1. The NixOS console.colors use a different set again (11111E, E12541, 14C67B, FFAC7D, 7270FF, FD8DFF, 75DFED, A4B1E3 / 474B77, DE6876, 63D961, FFDA8D, AAA9FA, E5A5FB, BEEDF8, DBE2FB). Dunst uses stock Catppuccin Macchiato colours (#8AADF4 blue, #EED49F yellow, #ED8796 red) on #0D0D1680. The flameshot uiColor is #1435c7, and the betterlockscreen accent is d23c3d. Catppuccin flavours are also mixed: catppuccin/nix is set to macchiato + blue on both system and HM, GTK uses mocha-lavender, the cursor is macchiato-dark, and spicetify is mocha.
aesthetic.color_pipeline: Static and hand-written. The catppuccin/nix flake (v26.05) is enabled globally at the NixOS level (flavor macchiato) and the Home Manager level (macchiato, accent blue), so it themes whatever ports it supports. On top of that, colours are hardcoded in qtile colors.py (a Python str subclass with a with_alpha() helper that appends an alpha hex byte), kitty.nix, dunst/settings.nix, betterlockscreenrc, system console.colors, and nvim lualine (bg #0f0f1c override). There is no matugen, wallust, pywal or stylix, and nothing generates colours from the wallpaper. The spicetify-nix catppuccin theme uses colorScheme mocha.
aesthetic.fonts: JetBrainsMono Nerd Font everywhere: the Qtile bar at fontsize 12, kitty at size 9, dunst as 'JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono 10', and the lockscreen as 'JetbrainsMonoNerdFont'. The TTY uses Terminus ter-116n.psf.gz with earlySetup. System fonts.packages: nerd-fonts.jetbrains-mono, fira-code, fira-code-symbols, liberation_ttf, noto-fonts, noto-fonts-cjk-sans, noto-fonts-color-emoji, proggyfonts, apl386. The bar also uses emoji battery glyphs.
aesthetic.icons_cursor_gtk_qt: GTK theme: 'catppuccin-mocha-lavender-compact+rimless' via pkgs.catppuccin-gtk.override { accents=[lavender]; size=compact; tweaks=[rimless]; variant=mocha }. Note that the upstream catppuccin/gtk project is archived, so this is a deprecated path. dconf sets color-scheme prefer-dark. The cursor is pkgs.catppuccin-cursors.macchiatoDark at size 24, but it is declared twice with different names: gtk.cursorTheme 'Catppuccin-Macchiato-Dark' and home.pointerCursor 'Catppuccin-Macchiato-Dark-Cursors'. Qt settings conflict: Home Manager sets qt.platformTheme.name and style.name to kvantum, while the system sets qt.style = 'adwaita-dark'. No icon theme is set explicitly.
aesthetic.geometry: Qtile Columns layout: border_width 2, margin 4, border_focus #8B8AF1, border_normal #0F0F1C. Screen gaps are Gap(4) on the bottom, left and right. The bar is size 24 with background #0F0F1C, margin [0,0,8,0] and widget backgrounds at alpha 0.9 (TaskList 0.8, Battery 0.7). Floating windows use border 2. Dunst: corner_radius 4, frame_width 2, frame_color #8AADF4, padding 8, horizontal_padding 14, separator_height 2, and a semi-transparent #0D0D1680 background. Kitty: window_padding_width 5, a separator-style tab bar at the bottom, and picom opacity-rule 95% for class kitty. The dropdown terminal is 90%x90% at x/y 0.05 with opacity 0.95. Windows have no rounded corners, no blur and no shadows.
aesthetic.animations: Only picom fading: fading = true, fade-in-step 0.02, fade-out-step 0.05, fade-delta 5. There are no bezier curves because there is no Hyprland. The system installs picom-pijulius (an animation fork of picom), but picom.conf has no animation settings. .xinitrc starts 'picom -f --backend glx' on host Bacon and '--backend xrender' on the other hosts.
aesthetic.wallpapers: A single bundled assets/wallpaper.png, linked to ~/assets/wallpaper.png and applied through Qtile Screen(wallpaper=..., wallpaper_mode='fill'). There is also a bundled assets/lockscreen.png for betterlockscreen, plus banner.png and a custom-coloured NixOS logo SVG. I found no attribution or licence for the wallpaper or lockscreen images and could not verify where they came from.
aesthetic.vibe: Clean, dark and understated: a deep navy base with periwinkle and lilac accents and flat, square-ish tiling with small 4px gaps. It looks coherent and pleasant but minimal, and it is not 'cute' in the modern rice sense: no rounded windows, no blur, no animations, a plain 24px text bar, and no launcher UI. The cute touches are small: the lockscreen texts ('OwO what's this?', 'beep boop...', 'Oh no!'), Greek-letter workspaces (ζπδωλσς), a boxed two-line zsh prompt, a tree-style fastfetch and an ASCII-art /etc/issue. The engineering (flake structure, CI, VM screenshot test) is more polished than the visuals. For a pastel Hyprland rice, the palette and the tooling are worth taking, not the visual design.

components.compositor: Qtile window manager on X11 (not Wayland), pinned via nixpkgs-qtile-0-36 with tests disabled, plus picom as the X compositor (fading only). Started with startx; there is no display manager.
components.bar_or_shell: The built-in Qtile bar (home/qtile/src/bar.py). Widgets in order: GroupBox (line highlight), Spacer, TaskList (text only, uniform width), Spacer, Prompt, Mpris2 (Spotify only), Battery (removed on desktop chassis, detected via hostnamectl), Net (bits, ↓↑), Memory (click opens btop in a 1720x860 kitty), MemoryGraph, CPUGraph, ThermalZone (hardcoded thermal_zone5), Spacer, Volume, Clock ('%A, %b %-d %H:%M:%S'), Spacer, QuickExit (⏻). A Systray is inserted at index 12 on screen 0 only. Two screens each get a bar.
components.launcher: No real launcher. The Qtile Prompt widget is triggered with spawncmd (mod+r). No rofi, fuzzel or wofi.
components.notifications: dunst via the Home Manager services.dunst module (settings.nix): corner_radius 4, frame 2, background #0D0D1680, and a Catppuccin Macchiato foreground per urgency. Timeouts are 10, 15 and 30 seconds. Left and middle click run the action; right click closes all.
components.lock_idle_logout: betterlockscreen (i3lock-color) via Home Manager services.betterlockscreen with arguments ['-u ~/assets/lockscreen.png'], plus a custom betterlockscreenrc (lock_timeout=300, dim_level 40, blur_level 1, white ring, red d23c3dff for wrong/keyhl, locktext 'OwO what's this?', veriftext 'beep boop...', wrongtext 'Oh no!', time_format %H:%M:%S). mod+l locks. security.pam.services.i3lock is enabled. Logout is the Qtile QuickExit widget, and mod+ctrl+q shuts Qtile down. There is no separate idle daemon; I did not verify the exact xss-lock wiring.
components.wallpaper_tool: Qtile's built-in Screen wallpaper setting (mode fill). feh is enabled through programs.feh but is not used for the wallpaper.
components.terminal: kitty (home/kitty.nix): JetbrainsMono Nerd Font at 9, 16-colour custom palette, background #1A1C31, foreground #CAD3F5, cursor #82E3F8, selection #A7A5FB, separator tab bar ' | ' at the bottom, window padding 5, 820x460 initial size, audio bell off. Also a Qtile ScratchPad dropdown kitty on mod+shift+space.
components.shell_prompt: zsh with oh-my-zsh (plugins git and ssh-agent) and a custom 'sigma' theme. It is a two-line box prompt, ┌─[user@host] - [~/path] - [git branch +] - [history#] then └─[$], with RPROMPT [%*]. Plugins are pinned with fetchFromGitHub: zsh-syntax-highlighting 0.8.0, zsh-autocomplete 23.07.13 and wakatime. Also zoxide and direnv (nix-direnv). Bash is configured as well.
components.editor: Neovim 0.12 via programs.neovim with lazy.nvim and a Lua config (catppuccin colorscheme, which is skipped when TERM=linux; lualine with bg #0f0f1c; telescope; nvim-tree; toggleterm; treesitter; LSP). LSP servers come from extraPackages: nil, lua-language-server, pyright, clangd, typescript-language-server, haskell-language-server ghc984 and, per the latest commit, qmlls.
components.file_manager: Thunar, with gvfs and tumbler enabled. The README mentions Ranger, but it is not in the packages.
components.fetch: fastfetch with a custom config.jsonc: a tree layout using ├/└ box characters, a ' ➜ ' separator, grouped OS/KRN/PKG/UPT, HW/CPU/RAM/GPU/DSK and WM/TRM/SHL/EDR, and the logo in light_blue/bright_blue.
components.login_boot: No display manager (services.xserver.displayManager.startx). GRUB on EFI with gfxmodeEfi 1920x1280x32 (1920x1200x32 on Sigmachine). catppuccin/nix macchiato is enabled at the system level, so GRUB and TTY ports may be themed; I did not verify which ports are active. There is no Plymouth; consoleLogLevel is 0 and initrd.verbose is false, for a quiet boot. The custom /etc/issue is ASCII art plus 'Web browsers are useless here.' and a yellow 'Welcome.'. The console palette is set by hand with Terminus.
components.extras: spicetify-nix (catppuccin theme, mocha; extensions fullAppDisplay, hidePodcasts, playNext, adblock, wikify). Flameshot from pkgs-stable (uiColor #1435c7, Print runs 'flameshot gui --clipboard'). btop with the TTY theme, rounded_corners and braille graphs. tmux (mouse, base-index 1). A custom qwerty-fr xkb layout packaged as a Nix derivation. polkit-gnome as a systemd user service. TLP with battery charge thresholds 30–70% on the ThinkPad. Also wakatime, vesktop, element and figma-linux.

standout_features: screenshot.nix builds a NixOS VM test with pkgs.testers.runNixOSTest that boots the real system modules (the lightweight 'Gha' host) in QEMU at 1920x1200 with virtio-gpu. It waits for the Qtile IPC socket, spawns kitty windows running fastfetch and cbonsai --seed=4 through 'qtile cmd-obj', positions them with xdotool, and calls machine.screenshot(). The update-screenshot.yml GitHub Action builds it on every push and commits screenshot.png, so the README screenshot is always generated from the actual config.

A 'Gha' nixosConfiguration that uses system/minimal.nix and home/minimal.nix with a fake root filesystem, used as a cheap CI and screenshot target, alongside the full hosts Sigmachine, Bacon and Toaster.

A mk-system helper that returns (lib.nixosSystem conf) // { inherit conf; }. Exposing the module list lets other derivations, such as the VM screenshot test, reuse exactly the same modules and specialArgs.
A single Python palette module with a Color(str) subclass whose with_alpha(0.9) appends a hex alpha byte, used by every bar and layout colour.
A chassis-aware bar: it parses hostnamectl for 'Chassis:' and drops the Battery widget on desktops.
A Qtile ScratchPad dropdown kitty (90%, opacity 0.95, stays visible when focus is lost) on mod+shift+space.
Greek-letter workspace names ζπδωλσς mapped to keys 1–7.
Cute betterlockscreen strings: 'OwO what's this?', 'beep boop...', 'Oh no!'.
A tree-style fastfetch layout using ANSI escape sequences in the keys (\u001b[0m├\u001b[34m KRN) with a ' ➜ ' separator.
A fully themed TTY: hand-picked console.colors, Terminus font with earlySetup, and an ASCII-art /etc/issue. nvim skips the Catppuccin colorscheme when TERM=linux.
A custom keyboard layout (us_qwerty-fr) packaged as a Nix derivation and wired into both xserver.xkb.extraLayouts and ~/.config/xkb.
git-hooks.nix pre-commit (nixpkgs-fmt) exposed as checks, with the devShell inheriting the shellHook, plus a CI 'nix flake check' workflow.
structure_install: Flat flake repo with these parts. flake.nix defines the nixosConfigurations Sigmachine (ThinkPad P16s Intel Gen2 via nixos-hardware), Bacon (Intel desktop with NVIDIA), Toaster, and the minimal Gha. hardware/<host>.hardware-configuration.nix holds per-host hardware. system/ holds the shared NixOS module default.nix, per-host _<host>.nix overrides, minimal.nix, polkit.nix, qwerty-fr.nix and issuerc. home/ is Home Manager with one directory or .nix file per program (qtile/src/*.py, picom, dunst, kitty.nix, gtk.nix, cursor.nix, betterlockscreen, zsh, nvim, fastfetch, tmux, btop, bash, flameshot.nix, git.nix, extra_files.nix). assets/ holds the wallpaper, lockscreen, banner and screenshots, and screenshot.nix is the VM screenshot test. Home Manager runs as a NixOS module (useGlobalPkgs, useUserPackages) with catppuccin.homeModules and spicetify-nix modules. Raw configs such as the Qtile Python, picom.conf, betterlockscreenrc and fastfetch jsonc are linked with home.file rather than generated from Nix. To install, run 'sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#<Host>' after editing the username and hardware config, then use startx. The README also describes a legacy non-Nix path ('cp -r .* ~', or a bare clone of the repo as $HOME), but it no longer matches the tree: there are no dotfiles outside home/ except .xinitrc and .inputrc. There is no Arch or other-distro support, and no install script.
nix_patterns: The flake has multiple nixpkgs inputs: nixos-unstable as the main set, nixos-25.11 as pkgs-stable (used for flameshot via extraSpecialArgs), and a nixpkgs commit pinned only for Qtile 0.36 (overrideAttrs dontUsePytestCheck = true).
nixpkgs.pkgs is injected into the modules ({ nixpkgs.pkgs = pkgs; }) with allowUnfree set at import time.

A mk-system { hostname, hasHostSpecific, specific-modules, base, home-base } helper derives ./system/_<host>.nix and ./hardware/<host>.hardware-configuration.nix from the lowercased hostname, and exposes conf through // { inherit conf; }.

Home Manager runs as a NixOS module with useGlobalPkgs and useUserPackages. users.${username}.imports = [ catppuccin.homeModules.catppuccin spicetify-nix.homeManagerModules.spicetify home-base ]. extraSpecialArgs carries username, system, pkgs-stable and spicePkgs.
catppuccin/nix is pinned to a release tag (ref v26.05) and enabled at both levels (nixosModules and homeModules, flavor macchiato, accent blue).
nixos-hardware modules are used per host (lenovo-thinkpad-p16s-intel-gen2, common-cpu-intel, common-pc-ssd).
Home Manager uses osConfig to decide packages (it adds pamixer and pavucontrol only if osConfig.services.pipewire.enable).
Per-host overrides use lib.mkForce (Toaster disables pipewire, docker, steam and libvirtd).
git-hooks.nix pre-commit check (nixpkgs-fmt) is exposed in checks.<system>, with devShell inheriting its shellHook, and formatter = nixpkgs-fmt.
pkgs.testers.runNixOSTest is used as a screenshot generator (packages.screenshot-system) and built in GitHub Actions.
Custom packages are exposed as flake outputs (packages.qwerty-fr, packages.qtile).
Nix settings: auto-allocate-uids, cgroups, uid-range, keep-outputs/derivations, auto-optimise-store, and gc --delete-older-than 90d.
It does not use stylix, disko, sops/agenix or impermanence.

    socket_file = "/home/${username}/.cache/qtile/qtilesocket.:0"
