The default is 'orichalcum' (the TEMPLATE and snowfire hosts), the author's fork of UwUnicorn: base00 #1a181a, base01 #262326, base02 #302c30, base03 #463f47, base04 #bfaab7, base05 #dbd7da, base06 #dbd7da, base07 #faf7f9, base08 #da4747, base09 #fd6d35, base0A #ffa846, base0B #fbc024, base0C #8049d5, base0D #b368ec, base0E #e27fc6, base0F #e64464. That is warm orange/gold/magenta on near-black. The user-level fallback theme is 'io' (same darks, base08 #de5b44, base0B #c965bf, base0C #9c5fce, base0D #0e85b9, base0E #6ac38f). Pastel options in the repo: fairy-floss (00 #343145, 01 #464258, 02 #6A6483, 03 #422013, 04 #9673D3, 05 #A0A0C0, 07 #F8F8F0, 08 #CC6666, 09 #FFEA00, 0A #C2FFDF, 0B #55b3cc, 0C #8295D6, 0D #FFB8D1, 0E #C5A3FF, 0F #96CBFE); uwunicorn (00 #241b26, 01 #2f2a3f, 02 #46354a, 03 #6c3c62, 04 #7e5f83, 05 #eed5d9, 07 #e4ccd0, 08 #de5b44, 09 #e39755, 0A #a84a73, 0B #c965bf, 0C #9c5fce, 0D #6a9eb5, 0E #6ac38f, 0F #a3ab5a); catppuccin-mocha (the standard values, e.g. 00 #1e1e2e, 08 #f38ba8, 0E #cba6f7, 07 #b4befe). The full theme list includes alph, ashes, 10 atelier-*, ayu-dark, bespin, caret, catppuccin-frappe/mocha, darkmoss, doom-one, dracula, ember, emil, eris, eva, everforest, fairy-floss, gigavolt, 4 gruvbox, helios, henna, horizon-dark, io, isotope, manegarm, material-vivid, miramare, monokai, nord, oceanic-next, old-hope, orichalcum, outrun-dark, selenized/solarized dark and light, spaceduck, stella, summerfruit-dark, tomorrow-night, twilight, ubuntu, uwunicorn, windows-95, woodland, xcode-dusk.
aesthetic.color_pipeline: Stylix (nix-community/stylix) with base16.nix. Each modules/themes/<name>/default.nix is a flat attrset: scheme, slug, author, description, polarity, backgroundUrl, backgroundSha256, base00..base0F. It is passed directly as stylix.base16Scheme, and stylix.image = pkgs.fetchurl { url = theme.backgroundUrl; sha256 = theme.backgroundSha256; }. The theme option is a lib.types.enum built from builtins.readDir ../../themes, so adding a folder adds a valid option. It is set system-wide (systemSettings.stylix.theme) and the HM default inherits from osConfig. stylix.autoEnable = false; targets are opted in explicitly: alacritty, kitty, gtk, kde, qt, console, chromium. Anything Stylix doesn't cover is templated by hand: Hyprland borders/groupbar, ashell TOML, fuzzel, fnott, hyprlock (using base07-rgb-r/g/b), and nwggrid bg all read config.lib.stylix.colors.baseXX, with alpha added as a hex suffix ('bf', 'e6', '88'). Mustache templates rendered by config.lib.stylix.colors { template = ...; } produce ~/.config/qt5ct/colors/oomox-current.conf, ~/.config/Trolltech.conf, ~/.config/kdeglobals, and a Doom Emacs theme (doom-stylix-theme.el.mustache). ~/.currenttheme records the active slug. 'phoenix refresh' (bound to SUPER+CTRL+R) runs the post-hooks. Changing a theme means a rebuild; there is no runtime wallpaper-to-colour generation (no matugen/wallust/pywal).
aesthetic.fonts: Monospace: FiraCode Nerd Font (pkgs.nerd-fonts.fira-code). Serif and sans: Fira Sans. Emoji: Twitter Color Emoji. Stylix sizes: terminal 18, applications 12, popups 12, desktop 12. Fuzzel uses '<mono>:size=20'. fnott uses title size 18, summary 15, body 14. Hyprland misc.font_family is the monospace font. Hyprlock labels use size 25 ('Screen Locked') and 20 ($TIME12). Kitty sets modify_font 'cell_width 90%'.
aesthetic.icons_cursor_gtk_qt: Cursor: quintom-cursor-theme, 'Quintom_Snow' on dark polarity and 'Quintom_Ink' on light, size 36, applied with 'hyprctl setcursor' in exec-once. Icons: papirus-icon-theme (lib.hiPrio), plus kdePackages.breeze and breeze-icons. GTK via the Stylix gtk target (nwggrid is started with '-g adw-gtk3'). Qt via the Stylix qt and kde targets plus hand-templated oomox/qt5ct colours, Trolltech.conf and kdeglobals. QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt5ct is commented out.
aesthetic.geometry: general: layout master, border_size 0, gaps_in 14, gaps_out 14, resize_on_border true. col.active_border is a rainbow gradient across base08, 09, 0A, 0B, 0C, 0D, 0E, 0F at 270deg (a solid base0B in performance mode), but border_size is 0, so it is effectively invisible. col.inactive_border is base02. decoration: rounding 0, dim_inactive true, dim_strength 0.15, dim_special 0.0, shadow enabled (default params). blur: size 10, passes 3, ignore_opacity true, contrast 1.17, brightness 0.65 on dark and 1.45 on light, xray/special/popups enabled. Opacity: alacritty and kitty 0.80 (the modules' own default is 0.85, overridden with mkOverride 40), emacs 80, windowrule opacity 0.80 for Zed, pavucontrol, Element, discord, Logseq, KeePassXC, Nautilus; browsers go to 1.0 when fullscreen. Fuzzel: bg base00+'bf', border width 0, radius 0. fnott: bg base00+'e6', border-size 0, min-width 520, bottom-right. ashell: opacity 0.7, background base00+'88', and a source patch sets every radius (sm/md/lg/xl) to 0 and all border widths to 0. hyprlock: background = screenshot, blur_passes 4, blur_size 5, noise 0.0117, contrast 0.8916, brightness 0.8172, vibrancy 0.1696. Input field 200x50, outline 3, rounding -1 (pill), dots_size 0.33, fail_transition 300. Scratchpads float at 80% x 85%; chat at 85% x 90%.
aesthetic.animations: bezier: 'wind, 0.05, 0.9, 0.1, 1.05'; 'winIn, 0.1, 1.1, 0.1, 1.0'; 'winOut, 0.3, -0.3, 0, 1'; 'liner, 1, 1, 1, 1'; 'linear, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0'. animation: 'windowsIn, 1, 6, winIn, popin'; 'windowsOut, 1, 5, winOut, popin'; 'windowsMove, 1, 5, wind, slide'; 'border, 1, 10, default'; 'borderangle, 1, 100, linear, loop' (a rotating rainbow border, wasted because border_size is 0); 'fade, 1, 10, default'; 'workspaces, 1, 5, wind'; 'windows, 1, 6, wind, slide'; 'specialWorkspace, 1, 6, default, slidefadevert -50%'. layerrules: 'animation popin 80%' for ashell-main-layer and notifications, 'animation fade' for nwggrid. Everything is disabled when performanceOptimizations = true.
aesthetic.wallpapers: None are bundled. They are hotlinked per theme from third-party wallpaper aggregators and pinned by sha256: orichalcum https://w.wallhaven.cc/full/m3/wallhaven-m3m1yk.png; fairy-floss wallhaven-rrgydw.jpg; uwunicorn r4.wallpaperflare.com (fantasy forest artwork); catppuccin-mocha images7.alphacoders.com/126/1266081.jpg; io images.hdqwalls.com 'aurora-s-embrace...anime'. These are unlicensed, uncredited third-party (largely anime/digital) art, and link rot is common enough that the author wrote modules/themes/background-test.sh to curl --head every URL. The orichalcum README's 'Background Link' points to a wallpapers.com webp that does not match the backgroundUrl actually used. The wallpaper is applied with hyprpaper (a generated hyprpaper.conf that preloads stylix.image) and reused as the sddm-astronaut background.
aesthetic.vibe: Clean, sharp and 'tiling-purist'. With zero rounding, zero borders, 14px gaps, heavy dark blur (brightness 0.65), 80% translucent terminals, dimmed inactive windows and an iced-based ashell bar patched to be fully square, it reads as a polished but austere Hyprland desktop, not a cute one. The default orichalcum palette is warm sunset (gold/orange/magenta on #1a181a). Cuteness only comes from choosing fairy-floss, uwunicorn or catppuccin. There are no custom widgets, dashboards, rounded pills or bespoke QML/AGS shell. Its strength is breadth and consistency: every app, including Emacs, Qt/KDE, SDDM, lockscreen, launcher and notifications, follows one base16 scheme and switches with a rebuild. Polish rating for a pastel rice: medium. It is an excellent engineering reference but a weak visual reference. I did not view desktop.png, so this is judged from the config rather than the screenshot.

components.compositor: Hyprland v0.52.2 from its flake (inputs.hyprland, submodules=true). System side: programs.hyprland with xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland. User side: HM wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings, with systemd.enable and systemd.variables ['--all']. Master layout. Portals: hyprland plus xdg-desktop-portal-termfilechooser (FileChooser goes to yazi). Plugins: none. iio-hyprland (patched for hyprpaper) handles auto-rotation.
components.bar_or_shell: ashell (a Rust/iced Hyprland bar), with a local ashell.patch that hides special workspaces, sets all radii to 0, removes borders, and moves the layer from Bottom to Top. It is launched as 'WGPU_BACKEND=gl ashell'. Config ~/.config/ashell/config.toml: modules left [AppLauncher, SystemInfo], center [Workspaces], right [Clock, Settings, Tray]; clock '%a %d %b %H:%M:%S'; scale_factor 1.25; CPU/mem/temp warn and alert thresholds. Waybar appears only in leftover layerrules and blurls; it is not installed. No quickshell, AGS, astal or eww.
components.launcher: fuzzel (programs.fuzzel, font size 20, show-actions, square, bf alpha) on SUPER+code:47 (semicolon). It is also the dmenu backend ('fuzzel -d') for networkmanager_dmenu (SUPER+I), keepmenu (SUPER+P) and hyprprofile-dmenu (SUPER+SHIFT+P). nwg-launchers nwggrid is a full-screen app grid on release of SUPER_L (bindr), started through an nwggrid-wrapper with '-o 0.55 -b <base00>'.
components.notifications: fnott (services.fnott): anchored bottom-right, top-down stacking, min-width 520, bg base00+e6. low urgency uses base03 text with a 2s default timeout; normal uses base07 with 3s; critical uses base08 with no timeout. Dismiss with SUPER+X, dismiss all with SUPER+SHIFT+X. The obs-notification-mute-daemon SIGSTOPs fnott while OBS runs. OSD: swayosd (services.swayosd, topMargin 0.5) for volume and brightness keys.
components.lock_idle_logout: hyprlock v0.9.2 (flake input): screenshot background with blur, a pill-shaped input field, and 'Screen Locked' and $TIME12 labels, coloured from Stylix. hypridle: lock_cmd 'pgrep hyprlock || hyprlock', before_sleep_cmd 'loginctl lock-session', lock at 165s, suspend at 180s. Lid switch and SUPER+CTRL+L lock the session; SUPER+SHIFT+S suspends. There is no dedicated logout menu (no wlogout/wleave); ashell's Settings menu provides lockCmd 'hyprlock &' and power. Layers use 'abovelock 2' so ashell and notifications show above the lock.
components.wallpaper_tool: hyprpaper (a generated hyprpaper.conf with preload and wallpaper = ,<stylix.image>). No swww, animated transitions or wallpaper picker.
components.terminal: Alacritty is the default (userSettings.terminal enum [alacritty kitty]). Kitty is also enabled and is used for yazi and the file chooser (TERMCMD='kitty --class=filechoose_yazi'). Both are coloured by the Stylix targets at 0.80 opacity. Kitty adds cell_width 90% and ctrl+=/- font-size keybindings.
components.shell_prompt: zsh with autosuggestions, syntax highlighting and the zsh-nix-shell plugin, plus a hand-written prompt. PROMPT: ' ◉ %U%F{magenta}%n%f%u@%U%F{blue}%m%f%u:%F{yellow}%~%f' then a newline and ' %F{green}→%f '. RPROMPT: a rainbow bar-graph glyph run '▂▄▆█▆▄▂' in red/yellow/green/cyan/blue/magenta/white. Aliases: ls='eza --icons -l -T -L=1', cat='bat', htop='btm', ranger='yazi', ','='comma'. No starship or oh-my-posh.
components.editor: Emacs (emacs-overlay) with a Stylix-generated doom-stylix-theme.el from a mustache template and a configurable opacity. The snowfire host sets editor = 'zed'. VSCodium and neovim (vi/vim aliases) are also configured.
components.file_manager: yazi, heavily keymapped, with the git, sudo, piper and yatline plugins, custom Nerd Font dir icons, and powerline-style yatline separators. It runs as a special-workspace scratchpad (SUPER+F) and as the GTK/portal file chooser through xdg-desktop-portal-termfilechooser. Nautilus appears only in opacity rules.
components.fetch: None found in the files I read. No fastfetch, neofetch or pfetch config is present in the tree.
components.login_boot: SDDM (kdePackages.sddm, wayland.enable, enableHidpi) with the sddm-astronaut theme, overridden with background = config.stylix.image, ScreenWidth 1920, ScreenHeight 1080 and blur false. A custom systemd 'sddm-avatar' service copies ~/.face.icon into /var/lib/AccountsService/icons before SDDM starts. The Stylix console target is enabled. I did not verify any bootloader theme or Plymouth; none appears in the tree listing.
components.extras: hyprshade with a GLSL grayscale shader ('scg' toggle), wlsunset through the 'sct <temp>' script, hyprpicker (SUPER+C copies the hex), grim/slurp screenshots on the Print keycode 107 with region/output/clipboard variants, screenshot-ocr (SUPER+SHIFT+T), hyprnome for GNOME-style dynamic workspaces, cursor zoom on SUPER+=/-, libinput-gestures, ydotool/wtype, hyprpolkitagent, udiskie, blueman-applet, CachyOS kernel with the scx_lavd scheduler (chaotic-nyx), StevenBlack hosts blocklist, Brave policy module, qutebrowser with per-profile containers, Element/Discord in a chat scratchpad, KDE Plasma and GNOME modules as alternative desktops, and a declarative Godot/Blender settings applier.

standout_features: A global 'userSettings.hyprland.performanceOptimizations' boolean that switches off blur, shadows, animations, xray and layer blur, and forces opacity to 1.0 across Hyprland, alacritty, kitty, emacs, fuzzel and ashell in one place. The rainbow border also collapses to a solid base0B.

hyprgamemode script (SUPER+CTRL+G): reads decoration:blur:enabled to detect the current state. It then either uses 'hyprctl --batch' to zero animations, shadow, blur, gaps, border and rounding and kill ashell and hypridle, or restores the exact values by interpolating them from the Nix config (config.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings.*). Nothing is duplicated.

hyprprofiles: named workflow profiles (Default, Gamdev, Teaching, Tech) in ~/.config/hyprprofiles/<name>/start-hook.sh and exit-hook.sh, switched with 'hyprprofile <name>' or a dmenu picker. Hooks rebind keys at runtime (e.g. SUPER+S goes to a per-profile qutebrowser container) and switch the org-roam database. The current profile is persisted in ~/.hyprprofile.

Five special-workspace scratchpads (terminal, yazi, numbat calculator, btm, Element/Discord chat). Each bind runs 'exec' only if the client is missing (checked with hyprctl clients | grep) and then 'togglespecialworkspace'. The scratchpads are pre-spawned at login, floated, centered, sized 80% x 85%, and slide in with 'slidefadevert -50%'.

Themes are plain data: each theme folder is an attrset with base16 colours plus wallpaper URL and sha256. The option type is an enum generated from readDir, so dropping in a folder registers a theme, and background-test.sh checks all wallpaper links for rot.

The GTK/portal file picker is replaced with yazi in a floating kitty (xdg-desktop-portal-termfilechooser with yazi-wrapper.sh and a TERMCMD class rule), so every Save/Open dialog becomes a themed TUI.

Manual mustache templating through config.lib.stylix.colors for targets Stylix lacks (qt5ct oomox colours, Trolltech.conf, kdeglobals, a Doom Emacs theme), plus an '+alpha-hex' suffix convention for translucent fuzzel, fnott and ashell backgrounds.

Layer-shell polish: blur, xray and ignorezero for the bar, notifications and launcher; 'animation popin 80%' on the bar and notifications; 'order 66/67'; and 'abovelock 2' so the bar and notifications can render above hyprlock.

Multi-user and multi-host scaffolding: systemSettings.users and adminUsers generate users.users and home-manager.users. hosts/<name> directories are auto-discovered into nixosConfigurations. A private secrets flake input (git+file:///etc/nixos.secrets) keeps per-host secrets out of the public repo.

The phoenix wrapper CLI (sync, update, pull, build and push to attic, lock/unlock chown of the dotfiles, gc Xd), with each step wrapped in systemd-inhibit so the lid switch or idle can't interrupt a rebuild.
structure_install: Layout: flake.nix builds nixosConfigurations for every directory under hosts/ (duskfall, ori, snowfire, stardust, zenith, plus TEMPLATE, which is filtered out of builds by phoenix but not by the flake's readDir). Each host has default.nix (imports configuration.nix and hardware-configuration.nix, and maps every systemSettings.users entry to HM imports [./home.nix ../../modules/user]), configuration.nix (systemSettings.* toggles) and home.nix (userSettings.* toggles plus host monitor and AQ_DRM_DEVICES overrides). modules/system/* and modules/user/* are auto-imported recursively by an importAll helper in each default.nix. Every module exposes mkEnableOption-style toggles under systemSettings.<x> or userSettings.<x>. modules/themes/<name>/default.nix holds base16 attrsets plus a README with a screenshot link. Install (install.org) is manual only: clone to /etc/nixos (or set systemSettings.dotfilesDir), copy hosts/TEMPLATE to hosts/<hostname>, replace USERNAME/NAME/EMAIL, generate hardware-configuration.nix, then either set up /etc/nixos.secrets from the nixos-secrets-template repo or delete the secrets input, and run 'sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake /etc/nixos#<host>'. After that, use 'phoenix sync'. HM runs as a NixOS module (inputs.home-manager.nixosModules.home-manager), not standalone, so nothing here applies to Arch directly.
nix_patterns: The flake has no flake-parts. outputs builds nixosConfigurations with builtins.listToAttrs over builtins.readDir ./hosts. system is hardcoded to x86_64-linux.

nixpkgs is patched through (import nixpkgs {}).applyPatches with an empty patch list, as a hook for pulling in unmerged PRs. Overlays: rust-overlay, emacs-overlay, chaotic (nyx). pkgs-stable (nixos-25.11) is passed through specialArgs.
Home Manager is a NixOS module with extraSpecialArgs {pkgs, pkgs-stable, inputs}. HM users are generated from systemSettings.users. HM modules read osConfig (e.g. the Stylix theme default).

Custom option namespaces systemSettings.* and userSettings.*, with lib.mkIf cfg.enable gating. Precedence is handled with lib.mkOverride 40, mkForce and mkDefault (e.g. the Hyprland module forces terminal opacity).

Stylix is imported at system level (nixosModules.stylix) and the HM module is imported conditionally only when the system Stylix is off (a comment explains they conflict). stylix.autoEnable = false with explicit per-target enables. config.lib.stylix.colors {template, extension} is used for mustache templating.
The theme enum is derived from lib.filterAttrs over builtins.readDir ../../themes. Wallpapers use pkgs.fetchurl with a pinned sha256 per theme.
Hyprland and hyprlock are pinned to release tags from their own flakes, with inputs.nixpkgs.follows.

pkgs.writeScriptBin is used heavily for inline helper scripts (hyprgamemode, nwggrid-wrapper, sct, scg, workspace-on-monitor, suspend-unless-render, phoenix). pkgs.makeDesktopItem is used for launcher entries. ashell and iio-hyprland get local patches through overrideAttrs.
A secrets flake input (git+file:///etc/nixos.secrets) exposes hostSecrets.<host> modules. The attic binary cache is populated by 'phoenix build'.
Not used: disko, sops-nix/agenix, impermanence, flake-parts, nixos-anywhere (the last two are mentioned as future ideas in install.org).

key_snippets.purpose: Core Hyprland look: gaps, gradient border, blur, dim, beziers and animations (performance-gated)
Bezier curves and animation lines (overshoot popin, anticipation on close, looping border angle)
hyprgamemode: toggle eye-candy off, then restore the exact values from the Nix config
Theme-as-data format (pastel example); wallpaper pinned by URL + sha256
Theme selection as a readDir-derived enum; Stylix wiring; mustache templates for non-Stylix targets
Scratchpad pattern + layer-shell polish rules
key_snippets.excerpt:
''SUPER,Z,exec,if hyprctl clients | grep scratch_term; then echo "scratch_term respawn not needed"; else alacritty --class scratch_term; fi''
          "SUPER,Z,togglespecialworkspace,scratch_term"
          ''SUPER,F,exec,if hyprctl clients | grep scratch_yazi; then echo "scratch_yazi respawn not needed"; else kitty --class scratch_yazi -e yazi; fi''
          "SUPER,F,togglespecialworkspace,scratch_yazi"
        windowrulev2 = [
          "float,class:^(scratch_term)$"
          "size 80% 85%,class:^(scratch_term)$"
          "workspace special:scratch_term silent ,class:^(scratch_term)$"
          "center,class:^(scratch_term)$"
        layerrule = lib.optionals (!performance) [
          "blur,ashell-main-layer"
          "blur,launcher # fuzzel"
          "blur,notifications"
          "xray 1,ashell-main-layer"
          "ignorezero, ashell-main-layer"
          "ignorezero,notifications"
          "animation popin 80%, ashell-main-layer"
          "animation popin 80%, notifications"
          "order 66,ashell-main-layer"
          "order 67,notifications"
          "abovelock 2,ashell-main-layer"
          "abovelock 2,notifications"
        ];

weaknesses: NixOS-only. Every config is generated by Nix/HM from Stylix variables and there are no raw dotfiles, so nothing is directly reusable on Arch. The flake is also hardcoded to x86_64-linux.

Syntax risk on newer Hyprland: it uses 'windowrulev2', legacy 'blurls', old-style 'layerrule = blur,<ns>' strings and the 'workspaceopt,allfloat' dispatcher, and pins Hyprland v0.52.2. My unverified understanding is that the window- and layer-rule syntax was reworked after 0.52 and workspaceopt was removed earlier. Check the current Hyprland wiki before copying any of these lines.

Deprecated NixOS/HM options: services.xserver.displayManager.sddm (renamed to services.displayManager.sddm), programs.zsh.enableAutosuggestions (now autosuggestion.enable), programs.zsh.initExtra (now initContent), and pkgs.system (nixpkgs now prefers stdenv.hostPlatform.system). stylix.homeManagerModules may also have been renamed (not verified).
The rainbow 8-colour gradient border and 'borderangle ... loop' animation are defined but invisible, because general.border_size = 0. It is dead eye candy that still costs a timer.

Hardcoded, machine-specific values: the snowfire monitor layout and AQ_DRM_DEVICES=/dev/dri/card2:/dev/dri/card1, the 'asus::kbd_backlight' device, raw keycodes (code:107/148/232/255...), the attic cache name 'emmet', a host list hardcoded in phoenix-system-builder (marked FIXME, 'doesn't work at all'), SDDM ScreenWidth/Height fixed at 1920x1080, and dotfiles at /etc/nixos with root chown games. The secrets input 'git+file:///etc/nixos.secrets' breaks evaluation for anyone who hasn't created it, and install.org warns that the ori host ships the author's SSH keys.

Wallpapers are hotlinked, uncredited third-party art from wallhaven, wallpaperflare, alphacoders and hdqwalls. They have unclear licensing and break when a URL dies (hence background-test.sh), which breaks the build because fetchurl hashes are pinned. The orichalcum README's background link doesn't match its backgroundUrl.
Palette bugs: fairy-floss base03 = 422013 (dark brown) is nearly invisible as comment or dim text on the #343145 background. orichalcum reuses the uwunicorn screenshot in its README.

Fragile shell hacks: scratchpad checks use 'hyprctl clients | grep' instead of jq; 'sleep 5 && hyprctl keyword bind SUPER,S,...' in exec-once; obs-notification-mute-daemon polls every 10s and SIGSTOPs fnott; the btm bind echoes 'scratch_yazi respawn not needed' (copy-paste error); the KeePassXC center rule uses the wrong case ('KeepassXC'); and there are duplicate rules ('size 86% 85%' for Create new document, Nautilus opacity listed twice).
Aggressive idle: lock at 165s and system suspend at 180s, only 15 seconds apart. suspend-unless-render exists but isn't wired into hypridle.

The exec-once autostarts personal apps (protonmail-bridge, syncthing, element-desktop, ydotoold) in the shared WM module rather than per host, so the module is opinionated and heavy for anyone reusing it.
The ashell look is changed by patching the Rust source to force radius 0. This is brittle across ashell releases and the opposite of the rounded 'cute' direction.
It depends on chaotic-cx/nyx for the CachyOS kernel and overlays; I did not verify whether that project is still maintained. There is no disko, sops or impermanence, and install is manual only.
steal_list: Adopt the theme-as-data pattern for both distros. Keep one folder per theme holding base16 hex, polarity, a wallpaper URL or path with its hash, and author credit. On NixOS, feed it to stylix.base16Scheme and derive the option enum with readDir. On Arch, render the same file with tinted-theming's tinty/flavours or a small mustache step, so both distros share one palette source.
Use a single 'performance' or 'eco' flag that gates blur, shadows, animations, layer blur and every app's opacity. On Arch, generate a hypr source file (e.g. perf.conf) that the toggle swaps.

Port the hyprgamemode approach: a keybind that uses hyprctl --batch to zero animations, blur, gaps, rounding and borders and kill the bar and idle daemon, then restores values read from the canonical config instead of duplicating them.

Reuse the animation feel: winIn (0.1, 1.1, 0.1, 1.0) overshoot with popin for opening, winOut (0.3, -0.3, 0, 1) anticipation for closing, 'wind' (0.05, 0.9, 0.1, 1.05) for workspaces and moves, and specialWorkspace 'slidefadevert -50%'. For a cute rice, pair them with rounding of about 12 to 16 and a visible border_size of 2 to 3, so the base08..base0F 270deg gradient and 'borderangle, 1, 100, linear, loop' actually show as a pastel rainbow rotating border.

Build special-workspace scratchpads (terminal, file manager, calculator, system monitor, chat) that pre-spawn at login, float at 80% x 85%, and toggle with a respawn-if-missing guard. Use 'hyprctl clients -j | jq' rather than grep.
Replace the GTK file picker with yazi through xdg-desktop-portal-termfilechooser and a floating, centered terminal class, so every Open/Save dialog is themed.

Use layer-shell polish rules (updated to current syntax): blur, ignorezero and xray for the bar, launcher and notifications; popin 80% animation on the bar and notifications; and abovelock so the bar and notifications show over the lock screen.

Use hyprlock with a blurred screenshot background (blur_passes 4, size 5, noise 0.0117, contrast 0.8916, brightness 0.8172, vibrancy 0.1696), a pill input (rounding -1) and palette-driven check and fail colours.
Add hyprprofiles-style context profiles with start and exit hooks and a fuzzel picker, for switching browser profile, keybinds and notes DB per task.
Use the '+alpha-hex' convention (base00+'bf' or 'e6') for launcher and notification translucency, and mustache templates for apps Stylix/matugen lack (qt5ct colours, kdeglobals, editor themes).

Take the pastel palettes as starting points: fairy-floss (fix base03 to something like #716799 first), uwunicorn and catppuccin-mocha. Use dim_inactive 0.15 and blur brightness 0.65 on dark or 1.45 on light with contrast 1.17 for depth.

Borrow the small script ideas: 'sct <kelvin>' wlsunset wrapper, hyprshade grayscale toggle, SUPER+C 'wl-copy $(hyprpicker)', SUPER+= and SUPER+- cursor zoom via cursor:zoom_factor, swayosd for volume and brightness OSD, and the rainbow-bar RPROMPT glyphs '▂▄▆█▆▄▂' for a cute prompt accent.
Wrap rebuilds in 'systemd-inhibit --what sleep:idle:handle-lid-switch', like the phoenix wrapper, so a lid close or idle suspend can't interrupt nixos-rebuild or pacman/paru runs.

one_line: A single-user NixOS flake that uses flake-parts, the "dendritic" pattern, import-tree, Stylix, Niri, Waybar, fuzzel, dunst, sops and impermanence. It is well engineered and very active, but the look is a plain Gruvbox/Catppuccin-Latte theme (the README calls it "Lack of Aesthetics"). It does not use Hyprland at all.
freshness: Very active. flake.lock has inputs locked as recently as 2026-09-24 13:08 UTC, one day before this analysis. It tracks nixos-26.05, home-manager release-26.05 and stylix release-26.05. niri comes from nixpkgs (a comment says "nixpkgs' niri (26.04) instead of niri-flake's stale niri-stable (25.08)"). doc/upgrades/2605/NixOS-26.05.md records fixes from the 26.05 upgrade (an i686 openblas deadlock and the fish 4.3 frozen-theme migration). GitHub Actions CI (.github/workflows/nixos.yml) builds both hosts with determinate-nix-action@v3.15.2 and cachix-action@v16. The README screenshots are dated 2022 and 2024-04 (boar_2024-04-01_22-55.png, flexbox_2024-04-02.png), so they probably predate the move to Niri and do not show the current desktop. I could not verify this because I did not view the images.

aesthetic.palette: The colours come from Stylix base16. Dark mode (the default) uses gruvbox-dark-medium: base00 #282828, base01 #3c3836, base02 #504945, base03 #665c54, base04 #bdae93, base05 #d5c4a1, base06 #ebdbb2, base07 #fbf1c7, base08 #fb4934, base09 #fe8019, base0A #fabd2f, base0B #b8bb26, base0C #8ec07c, base0D #83a598, base0E #d3869b, base0F #d65d0e. Light mode, set through the NixOS specialisation `light`, uses catppuccin-latte: base00 #eff1f5, base01 #e6e9ef, base02 #ccd0da, base05 #4c4f69, base08 #d20f39, base0A #df8e1d, base0B #40a02b, base0D #1e66f5, base0E #8839ef, base0F #dd7878. I checked these against tinted-theming/schemes. Hardcoded extras: wlr-which-key uses bg #282828d0 / #eff1f5d0, fg #ebdbb2 / #4c4f69 and border #fabd2f / #df8e1d. The Waybar calendar uses pastel spans: months #ffead3, days #ecc6d9, weeks #99ffdd, weekdays #ffcc66, today #ff6699 (bold and underlined). The Niri rule that highlights a screen-cast target uses border active #f38ba8 (Catppuccin Mocha red), inactive #7d0d2d and shadow #7d0d2d70.
aesthetic.color_pipeline: Static base16 through Stylix; there is no matugen, wallust or pywal. `stylix.base16Scheme` points at `${pkgs.base16-schemes}/share/themes/gruvbox-dark-medium.yaml`, and `stylix.image` is set to a bundled PNG. `specialisation.light.configuration` swaps in catppuccin-latte, the light wallpaper and polarity "light" using lib.mkForce. It also overrides dunst icons (Papirus-Light), GTK prefer-dark, the neovim lualine theme and the k9s skin. It writes `/etc/specialisation` with the text "light", and scripts read that file at runtime (niri-set-wallpaper.sh). Home Manager modules detect the theme with `isLightTheme = osConfig.specialisation == {}`. You switch themes with the fish abbreviations `dark-theme = "nh os test --no-specialisation && niri-set-wallpaper"` and `light-theme = "nh os test --specialisation light && niri-set-wallpaper"`. Waybar CSS uses the GTK colour variables Stylix injects (@base01, @base02, @base08, @base0A, @base0B, @base0D). Neovim's Stylix target is disabled; it uses its own gruvbox plugin. Fish is themed by Stylix through base16-fish universal variables, and the 26.05 upgrade doc describes friction with this.
aesthetic.fonts: Monospace is Fira Code (pkgs.fira-code); fontconfig monospace fallbacks are "FiraCode Nerd Font", "Fira Code" and "JuliaMono". Sans is DejaVu Sans, serif is DejaVu Serif and emoji is Noto Color Emoji. Stylix sizes are small: applications 9, desktop 9, terminal 8, popups 9. The system also installs fira-code-symbols, font-awesome_5, font-awesome_6 and font-awesome. A Home Manager activation step runs nerd-font-patcher to patch Fira Code with Nerd Font glyphs plus a locally supplied, proprietary Font Awesome 6 Pro (`~/.local/share/fonts/Font Awesome v6.5.1`). The output goes to `~/.local/share/fonts/NerdPatched/FiraCodeFAPro`. wlr-which-key uses "Fira Code 14". A `font-smoke-test` script prints bold, italic, ligature and icon samples.
aesthetic.icons_cursor_gtk_qt: Icons are Papirus-Dark and Papirus-Light (stylix.icons.enable with light/dark variants). The cursor is Bibata-Modern-Ice at size 24 (pkgs.bibata-cursors). GTK is themed by Stylix, with gtk3 `gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme = true`. Qt uses `platformTheme.name = "qtct"` and `style.name = "kvantum"`; Qt is disabled with mkForce false in the light specialisation. lxappearance, qt5ct and qt6ct are installed for tweaking. QT_AUTO_SCREEN_SCALE_FACTOR=1 and QT_ENABLE_HIGHDPI_SCALING=1 are set.
aesthetic.geometry: Niri layout: border enabled with width 2 (default 4), gaps 4 (default 16) and shadow enabled with default settings. Default column width is 1/2; the preset widths are 1/2, 1/3 and 2/3. No corner radius is set anywhere (there is no geometry-corner-radius rule), so windows keep square corners. No blur is configured. prefer-no-csd = true. On the vertical monitors, raw KDL sets default-column-width to proportion 1.0. Waybar sits at the bottom with spacing 6. Each module group is drawn as an "island pill": background @base01, border-radius 9px, margin-top and margin-bottom 3px, label padding 0 9px, box padding 0 5px. Workspace buttons have padding 0 4px, margin 3px 2px and radius 9px, and the active one gets an @base02 pill. wlr-which-key: corner_r 8, border_width 2, padding 12, anchored centre, separator " → ", about 82% opaque (d0 alpha). Alacritty padding is x 5, y 4. swaylock-effects uses screenshots with effect-pixelate 10 and effect-blur "7x5".
aesthetic.animations: Nearly everything uses Niri defaults. The only setting is `animations.workspace-switch.enable = false`. There are no custom curves, springs or shaders.
aesthetic.wallpapers: Two bundled PNGs, gruvbox-dark-rainbow.png (185,977 bytes) and gruvbox-light-rainbow.png (192,946 bytes). They are duplicated in parts/features/desktop/theming/_wallpapers/ and parts/features/desktop/niri/_wallpapers/. They are set with swaybg (`-m fill`) by the niri-set-wallpaper script, which checks /etc/specialisation, and are also passed to stylix.image. The repo does not state their source or licence, and I did not verify the artwork's origin. `variety` (the wallpaper changer) is installed with an 86400 s change interval, but the Niri startup only runs swaybg.
aesthetic.vibe: Honestly, this is not cute or pastel. It is a plain, dense Gruvbox desktop for engineering work, and the owner's README section is titled "Lack of Aesthetics". Gaps are tight (4px), borders are thin (2px), windows have square corners and fonts are small (9pt). The bottom Waybar packs about 20 system-monitor modules (CPU, temperature, GPU, disk, Tailscale, Mullvad, DDC brightness and more) into rounded 9px pills. The cutest touches are the moon-phase emoji brightness icons (🌑🌘🌗🌖🌕), the pastel calendar tooltip colours, the Catppuccin Latte light mode and the ly display manager's "doom" fire animation. The code and workflow are highly polished; the visuals are clean but spartan. On cuteness I'd rate it about 3/10; on functional polish, about 8/10.

components.compositor: Niri, using `programs.niri.package = pkgs.niri` from nixpkgs (26.04), configured declaratively through sodiboo/niri-flake's `programs.niri.settings` plus raw KDL nodes for per-output layout. It uses named workspaces " a" and " 1" through " 10" pinned to outputs, the overview (Mod+o), dynamic cast (Mod+G, Mod+Shift+G), `block-out-from = "screen-capture"` for Bitwarden and OBS, focus-follows-mouse, and xwayland-satellite. Hyprland is not used; only `hyprmagnifier` is borrowed. `programs.sway.enable = true` is also set.
components.bar_or_shell: Waybar through Home Manager, as a systemd user service. There are two bar definitions: `main` on DP-1 and eDP-1 with left, centre and right sections, and `aux` on HDMI-A-1 and HDMI-A-2 with only the left and right sections. Left: niri/workspaces. Centre: systemd-failed-units, group/cpu (cpu, temperature, custom/cpu-profile-toggler), memory, disk, group/gpu, group/network (network, tailscale, custom/macgyver, mullvad), group/screens (backlight or ddcutil per monitor, nightlight), group/audio (pulseaudio in and out, mpris), bluetooth, group/power (battery). Right: privacy, custom/peon-ping, custom/dunst-dnd, custom/caffeinate, niri/language, clock with a year calendar, tray. There is no Quickshell, AGS or eww.
components.launcher: fuzzel with the default config (`programs.fuzzel.enable`), coloured only by Stylix. It is reused as the dmenu for the niri-pick-window window switcher (with icons), the niri-qalc calculator, networkmanager_dmenu, rofimoji (`selector = "fuzzel"`), cliphist-fuzzel-img and dunst's dmenu.
components.notifications: dunst with minimal settings (browser brave, `dmenu = "fuzzel --dmenu"`, follow mouse); styling comes from Stylix. There are Waybar do-not-disturb toggle and waiting-count modules, and dunstify is preferred in scripts.
components.lock_idle_logout: Locker: swaylock-effects (screenshots, pixelate 10, blur 7x5, show-failed-attempts, ignore-empty-password), guarded with `pgrep -x swaylock ||`. Idle: swayidle locks at 360 s, powers off monitors at 370 s through `niri msg action power-off-monitors` (with a resume command) and runs `systemctl suspend-then-hibernate` at 1800 s; before-sleep and lock events also run the locker. Logout: wleave (`programs.wleave.enable`), bound to Mod+Pause. A Waybar "caffeinate" module stops and starts the swayidle user service. Mod+Shift+X locks the screen and powers off the monitors.
components.wallpaper_tool: swaybg, started by a custom `niri-set-wallpaper` writeShellApplication script that pkills swaybg and chooses the image from /etc/specialisation. Stylix also gets the image. variety is installed but not autostarted.
components.terminal: Alacritty (padding 5x4, 100000-line history, `TERM=xterm-256color`, vi-mode keys remapped to j/k/l/; and a beam cursor in vi mode), coloured by Stylix. urxvt.nix and herdr (the author's own tmux-like agent multiplexer) also exist.
components.shell_prompt: Fish is the main shell with vi keybindings remapped to jkl; and the bang-bang plugin; Nushell is used for data work. Starship has transience enabled, a long explicit module format, and shell indicators 🐟 fish, 💩 bash and 🦀 nu. Atuin, zoxide and fzf are also installed.
components.editor: Neovim, heavily modularised (about 45 plugin sub-modules under parts/features/dev/neovim/_*). Plugins include gruvbox, lualine, noice, notify, telescope, treesitter, mason-lsp, dap, neotest, overseer (with nixos-rebuild templates), oil, nvim-tree, diffview, jj, obsidian-nvim and render-markdown. The Stylix neovim target is disabled in dark mode and forced on in light mode. The README mentions Avante, but I found no avante module in the tree.
components.file_manager: lf with pistol previews, plus a fish wrapper so that quitting changes to the current directory; Nautilus is the GUI file manager; broot is also installed.
components.fetch: No fetch module is in the tree. The README shows neofetch screenshots from earlier years (assets/neofetch-boar.png).
components.login_boot: The display manager is ly (`animation = "doom"`, `hide_borders = true`) with defaultSession niri, and /etc/ly/save.ini is persisted under impermanence. Boot uses systemd-boot with memtest86 and systemd in the initrd. There is no Plymouth and no GRUB theme. Storage is LVM on LUKS; numenor adds btrfs impermanence and wipes / at boot with a root-explode initrd service that keeps old roots for 30 days.
components.extras: cliphist (200 items, dedupe search 10) with the cliphist-fuzzel-img picker on Mod+p. rofimoji through fuzzel (emojis, math, currency and fontawesome6). Satty screenshot annotation (fullscreen, initial tool crop) through the niri screenshot action. wlr-which-key chord menu on Mod+w with nested submenus. wlsunset plus wluma nightlight. kanshi monitor profiles (numenor and numenor-movie). ddcutil brightness for external monitors. niri-invert-colors through wl-gammactl. peon-ping sounds for Claude/Codex. OBS scene scripts. Brave, Zen and Firefox (Stylix firefox target, profile main). k9s gruvbox-dark and gruvbox-light skins. btop, nvtop and isd TUIs launched from Waybar clicks. Spicetify is not used, and no Discord theme was seen.

standout_features: Dark/light switching with NixOS specialisations: `specialisation.light.configuration` uses lib.mkForce to swap the Stylix scheme (gruvbox-dark-medium to catppuccin-latte), the wallpaper, polarity, dunst icon theme, lualine theme and k9s skin, and writes `/etc/specialisation`, which runtime scripts read. You switch without a reboot using `nh os test --specialisation light`. A fish wrapper around nh fixes the systemd-boot default entry after switching while a specialisation is active.

wlr-which-key chord menu (Mod+w) generated from a Nix attrset through `pkgs.formats.yaml`, with nested submenus for Niri, Keyboard, OBS and Display. Its colours switch with the light/dark detection `osConfig.specialisation == {}`. It works under any wlroots-protocol compositor, including Hyprland.

The `niriBinds` generator builds Cartesian products of key prefixes (Mod, Mod+Ctrl, Mod+Shift, ...) and suffixes (directions and workspaces) into action names, with string substitutions. This cuts keybinding boilerplate a lot and uses vim-shifted j/k/l/; navigation.

A fuzzel window picker (niri-pick-window.sh) that uses the rofi extended-dmenu icon protocol (`label\0icon\x1f<icons>`). It resolves icons from the .desktop `Icon=` value and several app_id heuristics, then focuses the chosen window by index. It is easy to port to `hyprctl clients -j`.

A nightlight toggle that looks up coordinates offline from the active IANA timezone in /etc/zoneinfo/zone1970.tab (converting ISO 6709 to decimal) with no geolocation API, starts wlsunset and wluma together, and refreshes Waybar with `pkill -35 waybar` (signal = 1).
An invert-colours toggle that coordinates the single-client wlr-gamma-control between wl-gammactl and wlsunset, pausing and restoring the nightlight through a state file in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.

Waybar "island pill" CSS in which every rule is prefixed with `window#waybar` so it outranks the per-module ID rules Stylix injects. Groups use 0 inner spacing, so label padding alone controls spacing, and the active workspace gets a small @base02 pill instead of an underline.

Niri window rules that highlight the current screen-cast target in red (#f38ba8 active, #7d0d2d inactive, shadow #7d0d2d70) and hide Bitwarden and OBS from screen capture (`block-out-from = "screen-capture"`).

Auto-column service (niri-auto-column.sh): it reads `niri msg --json event-stream` and stacks new windows into a column on the vertical monitors, tracking known window IDs so focus changes do not trigger it again.

Dendritic architecture: import-tree auto-imports every file in parts/. Each feature file defines both `flake.modules.nixos.<x>` and `flake.modules.homeManager.<x>` and declares its own impermanence paths. Per-host facts are typed `dendrix.*` options (isLaptop, hasNvidia, hasAmd, isImpermanent, isBtrfs) rather than specialArgs.
Honest upgrade write-ups (doc/upgrades/*) and CI that builds each host with `--override-input secrets nixpkgs`, so a private secrets flake does not break public builds.
structure_install: Layout: flake.nix contains only the inputs and `inputs.flake-parts.lib.mkFlake ... imports = [(inputs.import-tree ./parts)]`. parts/modules.nix imports flake-parts.flakeModules.modules. parts/hosts.nix defines the `dendrix` options module, commonNixosModules (determinate, nur, impermanence, sops-nix, stylix, home-manager, niri-flake), commonHomeManagerSettings (useGlobalPkgs, useUserPackages, backupFileExtension \"home-manager-backup\", sharedModules = all homeManager modules) and a `mkHost` helper. It builds two hosts: flexbox, a laptop with NVIDIA PRIME offload on Intel (probably a Dell XPS 9700, going by xps-9700-mic-fixer.sh), and numenor, an AMD desktop with three LG 4K monitors (two rotated 90°) and btrfs impermanence. Host-specific files live in parts/_hosts/<host>/; the underscore prefix excludes them from import-tree. Features are organised as parts/features/{core,desktop,apps,dev,hardware,security,services}, with scripts in `_scripts/` or `scripts/` subfolders wrapped by `pkgs.writeShellApplication`. Every module is applied to every host, and behaviour is gated by `config.dendrix.*`. Install: manual and imperative, following doc/INSTALL.md (gdisk, LUKS, LVM, btrfs subvolumes root/nix/persist, nixos-generate-config, nixos-install). You then clone the repo, rename your user to `farlion` (\"because it's hardcoded\"), and build with `sudo nixos-rebuild boot --flake .#<host> --override-input secrets nixpkgs`. Day to day it uses `nh os switch` or `nh os build`, with the binary cache `workflow-nixos-config` on cachix. disko is not used (the docs say disko does not support dual boot). devenv.nix, devenv.yaml and .envrc provide a development shell. There is no Arch or other-distro path.
nix_patterns: flake-parts with `flake.modules.nixos.*` and `flake.modules.homeManager.*` deferred modules (flakeModules.modules), following the dendritic pattern (mightyiam/dendritic)
vic/import-tree auto-imports parts/; files and directories prefixed with `_` are excluded (for example _hosts, _scripts, _wallpapers)

Typed per-host options module (`options.dendrix.{hostname,isLaptop,isImpermanent,hasNvidia,hasAmd,isBtrfs,stateVersion,homeStateVersion}`) read as `config.dendrix` in NixOS and `osConfig.dendrix` in Home Manager
Home Manager as a NixOS module; all HM feature modules are injected through `home-manager.sharedModules`; HM is pinned to release-26.05 with nixpkgs following
Stylix (danth/stylix release-26.05): base16Scheme from pkgs.base16-schemes, a cursor, fonts, an image, icons (Papirus light/dark), and per-target overrides (firefox profileNames, neovim disabled)
A NixOS `specialisation.light` for the light theme, using lib.mkForce overrides and an /etc marker file
sodiboo/niri-flake `programs.niri.settings`, plus appending raw KDL via `inputs.niri.lib.kdl` (node/plain/leaf) to `programs.niri.config` for settings the flake does not expose

nix-community/impermanence: btrfs root wipe in an initrd systemd service (skipped on resume via `ConditionKernelCommandLine = ["!resume="]`, keeps old_roots for 30 days), with each feature declaring its own `home.persistence."/persist"` paths behind `lib.mkIf osConfig.dendrix.isImpermanent`
sops-nix and a private `secrets` flake input (`path:/home/farlion/code/nixos-secrets`) whose modules are merged in only when present; CI overrides it with nixpkgs
Determinate Nix module (flakehub `DeterminateSystems/determinate`)
An overlay exposing `unstable` (nixos-unstable with allowUnfree) as `pkgs.unstable`; NUR through `nur.modules.nixos.default`
`pkgs.writeShellApplication` with explicit runtimeInputs and script bodies read with `builtins.readFile` from separate .sh files, enforced as a code-style rule in AGENTS.md
`pkgs.formats.yaml {}` to generate the wlr-which-key config from a Nix attrset
A standalone `homeConfigurations.farlion` kept only so the `home-manager news` CLI works
GitHub Actions: determinate-nix-action, cachix-action, one job per host building `config.system.build.toplevel`
nix-index-database, nh, nix-ld and cachix modules under parts/features/core and parts/features/apps

key_snippets.purpose: Waybar island-pill CSS that outranks the rules Stylix injects
Stylix base theme plus light-mode specialisation (the theme-switch mechanism)
wlr-which-key chord menu generated from Nix, with theme-aware colours
Lock and idle chain (swaylock-effects plus swayidle with niri monitor power-off)
Compositor geometry and the screen-cast target highlight rule
Offline, timezone-derived nightlight (wlsunset plus wluma) with a Waybar signal refresh
key_snippets.excerpt:
# Coordinates come from the active IANA timezone (kept current by tzupdate),
# resolved offline via the tzdata table -- no geolocation API, no network.
ZONE_TAB=/etc/zoneinfo/zone1970.tab

main() {
	if pgrep -x wlsunset; then
		stop_nightlight
	else
		start_nightlight
	fi
	pkill -35 waybar
}

start_nightlight() {
	local coords
	if ! coords=$(timezone_coords); then
		notify-send wlsunset.sh "No coordinates for timezone $(current_timezone); skipping."
		return
	fi
	read -r latitude longitude <<<"$coords"
	wlsunset -l "$latitude" -L "$longitude" &
	systemctl --user start wluma.service
}

timezone_coords() {
	local iso
	iso=$(awk -v tz="$(current_timezone)" '$3 == tz {print $2; exit}' "$ZONE_TAB")
	[ -n "$iso" ] || return 1
	iso6709_to_decimal "$iso"
}

weaknesses: Not Hyprland and not a cute/pastel rice. The compositor is Niri, the theme is stock Gruvbox with Catppuccin Latte, windows have square corners, there is no blur, the only animation setting disables workspace switching, and fonts are 9pt. The README section is titled "Lack of Aesthetics".
NixOS only, with no Arch path. The whole setup is flake modules; only the shell scripts can be reused on other distros.

The username `farlion` is hardcoded throughout: users.nix, `home-manager.users.farlion` in theming.nix and fonts, `/persist/home/farlion` in the impermanence activation script, and `homeConfigurations.farlion`. INSTALL.md literally says to "change your name to `farlion` because it's hardcoded".
The flake input `secrets.url = "path:/home/farlion/code/nixos-secrets"` is an absolute local path, so the flake cannot be evaluated without `--override-input secrets nixpkgs`.

Host-specific values are hardcoded in shared modules: Waybar hwmon paths (`/sys/devices/platform/coretemp.0/hwmon/hwmon7/temp1_input`), GPU busy via `/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon1/...`, Bluetooth MACs and USB device serials in the pulseaudio format-icons, i2c bus numbers in ddcutil, monitor connector names in both niri and waybar, and a literal placeholder `hwmon-path = "TODO find me according to waybar docs..."` for the flexbox GPU temperature.
A Waybar key typo, `format-connnected-battery` (three n's), means the Bluetooth battery format never applies.

Several Waybar custom modules poll every second by spawning processes (`custom/nightlight` runs pgrep, `custom/caffeinate` runs systemctl is-active, `custom/dunst-dnd` runs dunstctl) instead of using signals or event streams, which is wasteful.

Stale documentation. The README points to a `home` directory and `specialisations/light/default.nix`, neither of which exists. INSTALL.md refers to `machines/<host>` and `home/git.nix`. DENDRITIC.md says gruvbox-dark-hard, but the code uses gruvbox-dark-medium. The README lists Avante, but I found no avante module. The README badge points to workflow/nixos-config. The screenshots are from 2022 and 2024.
The Font Awesome 6 Pro patch depends on a proprietary font placed by hand in ~/.local/share/fonts and patched imperatively during HM activation, which is neither reproducible nor redistributable.

The wallpapers are bundled twice (theming/_wallpapers and niri/_wallpapers) with no stated source or licence. The wallpaper is set by a pkill/swaybg/disown script rather than a supervised service (the comment says "until stylix supports it").
Startup hacks: `sleep 10 && systemctl --user restart xdg-desktop-portal` works around a portal timing issue (niri-flake#509), and a 0.05 s sleep-based column consume in niri-auto-column.
Committed build artefacts: `parts/features/dev/opencode-sync/src/__pycache__/*.pyc`.
A novelty fish function, `pirate`, runs curl with `--insecure` and a hardcoded tracking cookie.
Stylix themes fish through universal variables, which conflicts with impermanence and needed a manual `rm` after the fish 4.3 upgrade (documented in the 26.05 notes).
fuzzel and dunst are left almost at defaults (Stylix colours only), with no bespoke radius, padding or icon styling.
The only system is x86_64-linux, and there is no disko, so installation is fully manual.
steal_list: Implement the light/dark switch as a NixOS specialisation (Stylix scheme, wallpaper and polarity swapped with mkForce) that writes a marker file (/etc/specialisation). On Arch, mirror it with a state file in ~/.local/state, so the same scripts (wallpaper, bar reload) branch on one source of truth on both distros.
Detect the theme inside HM modules with `osConfig.specialisation == {}` so that app configs (for example a which-key menu or a launcher) pick pastel light or dark hex values at build time.

Adopt wlr-which-key (it works on Hyprland) as a Mod+w chord menu generated from Nix or YAML with nested submenus. Restyle it pastel with a translucent background (the d0 alpha trick), corner_r of 12 or more, border_width 2 and a cute separator.

Port the Waybar island-pill CSS pattern: prefix every rule with `window#waybar` to beat the rules Stylix or matugen inject, use 0 group spacing with per-label padding, and draw the active workspace as a pill. Raise the radius (for example 14px) and add pastel accents for a cuter look.
Reuse the pastel calendar tooltip spans (#ffead3 months, #ecc6d9 days, #99ffdd weeks, #ffcc66 weekdays, #ff6699 today) in the Waybar clock, which fit a cute palette immediately.
Port niri-pick-window.sh to Hyprland: swap `niri msg --json windows` for `hyprctl clients -j` and keep the .desktop icon resolution and the rofi extended-dmenu icon protocol into fuzzel.

Take the small fuzzel utilities as they are: a qalc calculator that copies the result and notifies, cliphist-fuzzel-img for clipboard images, rofimoji with `selector = "fuzzel"`, and networkmanager_dmenu with `dmenu_command = fuzzel --dmenu`.

Adopt the offline nightlight toggle (IANA timezone to coordinates from zone1970.tab, wlsunset plus wluma) and the gamma-aware invert-colours toggle. Refresh the bar with a real-time signal (`pkill -35 waybar` / `signal = 1`) instead of polling.

Use the Waybar custom modules for a friendly control centre: caffeinate (toggles the idle daemon), notification DnD with a waiting count, and systemd-failed-units (click opens journalctl in lnav). Use signals rather than 1-second intervals.
Use moon-phase emoji for brightness (🌑🌘🌗🌖🌕); it is a cute touch that is easy to reuse.

Idle chain: lock at 6 min, DPMS off at 6m10s with a resume command, and suspend-then-hibernate at 30 min. On Hyprland, use hypridle and hyprlock instead of swayidle and swaylock-effects, but keep the timings and the `pgrep -x locker ||` guard.

Mirror the privacy features on Hyprland: hide password managers from screen capture and highlight the window being shared. Niri has native rules for this; for Hyprland, check the current windowrule options before promising parity (not verified here).

Structure the Nix side dendritically: flake-parts plus import-tree, one file per feature holding both its NixOS and HM aspects, typed per-host options instead of specialArgs, `_`-prefixed folders for non-module assets, and writeShellApplication with scripts in separate files so shellcheck runs at build time.
Set up CI that builds every host's toplevel with `--override-input secrets nixpkgs` and pushes to cachix, so that private secrets never block public builds.
Add a `font-smoke-test` script (bold, italic, ligatures and Nerd Font glyphs) to verify font rendering after a theme change.
Use ly with the "doom" animation (or a pastel-coloured ly config) as a lightweight, distro-neutral display manager that works on both Arch and NixOS.
